item.title: Scouting New York Jets wide receiver Sterling Shepard
item.description: Taking a look at a veteran WR acquisition
item.content:encoded:
The Jets recently signed former Giants and Bucs receiver Sterling Shepard to their practice squad. Shepard has already been active a few times for the Jets. Today, we break him down in detail.

The 33-year old Shepard is listed at 5’10” and 194 pounds and was a second round pick out of Oklahoma in 2016. He has had a productive NFL career with 440 receptions for almost 5,000 yards and 25 touchdowns and although most of that production came early in his career, he has been a useful contributor over the last few seasons.

Background

Shepard was a four-star high school recruit and headed to Oklahoma in 2012. As a true freshman, he posted a 100-yard game in his second appearance. Over the course of the season, he started four games and caught 45 passes for 621 yards and three scores.

In 2013, he started 12 of 13 games and ramped up his production with 51 catches for over 600 yards and seven scores.

2014 saw him level up again, as he had over 900 receiving yards with a month of the season still remaining. However, injuries down the stretch limited him and he ended the year with 51 catches for 970 yards and five touchdowns. This was good enough for first team all-Big 12 recognition, though.

In his final college season, he was a first-teamer again and was also named as an all-American as he had 1,288 receiving yards on 86 catches, with 11 touchdowns. The season was highlighted by an overtime win over Tennessee where Shepard caught the game-tying and game-winning touchdowns.

Shepard was drafted by the New York Giants with the 40th overall pick in the 2016 draft and immediately made an impact with a touchdown in his first game and a 100-yard game the following week, leading to an all-rookie season.

Over his first five years, he established himself as a reliable producer, catching at least 57 passes and having over 650 receiving yards each year. He had 20 touchdowns and his highest single-season output for yardage was 872 in 2018.

During the next three seasons with the Giants, Shepard – who had signed a four-year extension ahead of the 2019 season – saw his career take a downturn due to injuries.

After a productive start to the 2021 season, Shepard missed several games and then suffered a season ending Achilles tear in December. Then, in 2022, he made his comeback and was again off to a decent start only to tear his ACL in week three.

He was back in 2023, but struggled to crack the rotation and ended up with just 10 catches for 57 yards as it looked like his career might be winding down.

In 2024, he ended up on the Bucs’ practice squad, where he reunited with his college teammate Baker Mayfield. It wasn’t long before he was elevated to the active roster and he ended up starting five times and racking up 32 catches for 334 yards and a score in 14 appearances in a bounceback campaign.

The Bucs re-signed him for 2025 and he was again a useful player with 39 catches for 371 yards and a touchdown in 13 games, despite only making two starts.

Shepard was without a team this year until preseason when he signed with the Texans. However, he was released in final cuts eight days later. The Jets added him to their practice squad in September and he was elevated for two games due to some injuries, catching two passes including a two-point conversion.

Let’s move onto some more in-depth analysis of what Shepard brings to the table, based on in-depth research and film study.

Measurables/Athleticism

Shepard lacks ideal size but has big hands and is strong. He posted 20 bench press reps at the scouting combine.

He also posted an impressive 41-inch vertical at the scouting combine, although the rest of his numbers, including a 4.48 in the 40-yard dash, were about average for his size. This was also over a decade ago.

Usage

Shepard has played in the slot 60 percent of the time at the NFL level but can still produce on the outside. In college he played outside in 2014 but in the slot in 2015 to showcase his versatility.

He’s also been an option on jet sweeps and end arounds with 17 carries for 109 yards and a touchdown in college and 36 carries for 274 yards and a touchdown in the NFL.

He played both running back and wide receiver in high school, while also playing basketball and participating in track and field events.

Deep threat

Shepard has a reputation as a possession receiver but has made plenty of downfield plays over the years and even led the Big 12 in yards per catch in 2014.

He hasn’t been as effective as a downfield threat in recent years as he was early in his career but has still made the occasional downfield plays here and there.

Hands

Shepard is regarded as a sure-handed receiver who has a 67 percent catch rate for his career.

He dropped 20 passes in his first three seasons but has improved his efficiency dramatically since then as he has never had more than five drops in any season since that time and had just one drop on 53 targets last year.

He has a good ability to adjust to the ball and make tough catches in traffic.

Shepard is also adept at going up to get it in fade situations and staying inbounds on sideline catches.

Routes

Shepard is an excellent route runner who deploys foot quickness, deception and strength to generate short area separation.

He can run a full route tree and is excellent at tracking and locating the ball early so he can compete for it.

Red zone

Shepard racked up 27 touchdowns in four years at the collegiate level but has been less of a red zone threat at the NFL level.

He had eight touchdowns as a rookie and has 26 in his career, but hasn’t had more than one in a season since 2020. Of those scores, 18 came from inside the red zone with eight inside the three-yard line, although only one of those eight was after 2020.

The Jets did use him in the red zone on this clutch game-tying two-point conversion, though.

After the catch

Shepard doesn’t break a ton of tackles but has the ability to turn upfield and dive for the marker or pylon, and can turn a short pass into a big play with his speed.

He has been a solid option on screen passes throughout his career, averaging nine yards per screen pass while in Tampa Bay.

He did not fumble in college but has four at the NFL level.

Blocking

Shepard has earned a reputation as a willing blocker who gives a great effort and takes pride in his technique. Former Giants general manger Dave Gettleman once said he was “a hell of a blocker”.

That effort was on display here as he hustled downfield to knock Josh Norman off a downfield tackle.

In the same game, he also sprang a long touchdown run with this excellent block. He was actually awarded a game ball for this performance despite just catching two passes for 17 yards.

He hasn’t been called for holding in his career but was flagged for an illegal crackback block and a couple of illegal block in the back penalties.

Physicality

Aside from his blocking, Shepard also showcases tenaciousness when running routes, carrying the ball and making catches in traffic. He is also good at fighting off press coverage.

He can take things a little too far at times, though, as he has six offensive pass interference penalties in his career, in addition to four for unsportsmanlike conduct or unnecessary roughness.

Special Teams

Shepard had some experience as a punt returner in college, as he fielded 30 punts and averaged 7.4 yards per return.

This came in handy in 2023 as the Giants had to use him as an emergency punt returner but he had just 10 yards on three returns with two fair catches and a muff.

He also fielded one kickoff in college and gained 27 yards on a kickoff return after a lateral at the NFL level.

Aside from the return game, he hasn’t really been used on special teams at the NFL level with just 20 special teams snaps in his career.

Instincts and Intelligence

Shepard is adept at finding the soft spot in zones and reading coverages, both in terms of pre-snap formations and the positioning of the player who is covering him.

His focus can let him down at times, as he has 10 pre-snap penalties in his career, including seven false starts.

Attitude

Shepard is regarded as an excellent locker room presence and a respected mentor who can be a vocal leader. He brings energy and intensity and has always been a popular teammate wherever he goes.

He has also shown toughness in overcoming some of the injury issues he has had to remain in the league and was awarded the Ed Block Courage award while with the Giants.

Shepard’s father also played in the NFL but died when he was just six years old.

Injuries

Shepard’s career was impacted significantly by his Achilles injury in 2021 and ACL tear in 2022, and he had also spent time on injured reserve with a turf toe in 2020.

He’s been banged up a lot during the rest of his career, though, with injuries to his hamstring, quad, calf, ankle and neck. He also had multiple concussions that caused him to miss time in 2019 and missed time due to a groin issues during his junior year with the Sooners.

Scheme Fit

As noted, Shepard is a slot receiver who would most likely be in a possession role but could play outside in a pinch.

He was in the rotation for the Lions and Bears games, playing primarily in the slot as he filled in for Omar Cooper.

During his NFL career, he has been a teammate of current Jets Geno Smith, Jack Heflin, Jimmy Morrissey and Dane Belton while with the Giants. In Smith’s lone start for the Giants, Shepard caught three passes for 56 yards.

Conclusions

Shepard has already proven he can step in and do a job with the Jets, although now that Tim Patrick is healthy and Omar Cooper and Adonai Mitchell should be about to return, it might be some time before he is needed again.

Having been elevated twice from the practice squad already, Shepard is eligible to be elevated one more time, after which he will need to be added to the 53-man roster if he is to play again.

While the Jets will hope that their receiver rotation remains intact for the rest of the year, we are all well aware that this may not be the case. It’s therefore nice to have a veteran option like this waiting in the wings and, even if he isn’t the player he once was, he seems like he still has something left in the tank.

item.title: 3 RBs the Titans could pursue next offseason
item.description: The Tennessee Titans need to be better at RB next season; taking a look at some potential veteran targets.
item.content:encoded:
The Tennessee Titans have the worst offense in the NFL. A big reason why is the lack of support they receive from the rushing attack. At 0-5, the Titans currently possess the 27th ranked rushing offense in the NFL.

Both Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears are on expiring contracts. It’s difficult to envision GM Mike Borgonzi re-signing either of them after the lackluster season they are having. If the Titans want to continue supporting Cam Ward, they should consider bringing in a veteran RB to aid the offense.

Let’s look ahead to some potential free-agent running backs the Titans can consider signing in 2027.

Brian Robinson Jr., Atlanta Falcons

Atlanta Falcons running back Brian Robinson Jr. has rushed for 210 yards and four touchdowns this season despite backing up Bijan Robinson. He’ll almost certainly be looking for an opportunity to be a feature back next offseason. Robinson probably isn’t a true bellcow, but he’s better than any ball-carrier the Titans have right now.

Zach Charbonnet, Seattle Seahawks

Zach Charbonnet is about to return for the Seattle Seahawks from a torn ACL injury he suffered during the playoffs last year. Everyone around the league will be monitoring his form once he’s back. The Seahawks don’t believe in signing RBs to second contracts. They made the grave mistake of letting Kenneth Walker III leave, and just drafted Jadarian Price with a first-round pick. Charbonnet will almost certainly hit the open market.

Chase Brown, Cincinnati Bengals

Chase Brown is probably the best running back currently playing on an expiring contract. Can the Cincinnati Bengals afford to re-sign him after designating so much money on offense to Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins? Probably not. Adding Brown would provide the Titans offense with a true dual-threat back, even if he’s currently struggling in 2026.

item.title: The Falcoholic Reacts Survey: Pressing issues
item.description: Adjustments are needed in Atlanta going into a daunting stretch against several contenders.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Falcons fans and fans across the country.

Losing to the Ravens served as a bit of a reality check for the Falcons. For as exceptional as they looked against Green Bay and New Orleans, they were outplayed for long stretches against one of the NFL’s top teams. It was somewhat encouraging that they were in position to win despite struggling in the trenches, not running the ball efficiently down to down, and Michael Penix Jr. being rattled under pressure.

A spirited effort only gets a team so far when both units are making critical mistakes. The offense can’t afford to barely be on the field in the first quarter. That puts the defense in a precarious position, particularly late in games when they have to tackle one of the most ferocious running backs in NFL history. While the defense can be commended for overachieving, it’s a group with glaring limitations that opposing top offenses will exploit.

The errors made in the loss to Baltimore should be fixable. The question is what is most pressing that will determine the Falcons’ chances against a multitude of dynamic offenses on the horizon. What do you think the Falcons must fix to stay on track to win the NFC South during what is considered the hardest part of their schedule?

Where do the Falcons need to improve?

Are you confident in the Falcons?

item.title: Rams make roster moves, try to figure out special teams
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams are making (needed) roster moves and more NFL news on a Thursday
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams added Blake Grupe as their new kicker (for now), and they’ve added some other players including cornerback Damarion Williams. Williams could be a signing to help while Jaylen Watson deals with his injuries, but Williams could also be someone to bolster L.A.‘s special teams.

Sean McVay said all options were on the table after their loss to the Buffalo Bills, and the Rams should leave no stone unturned.

Going into Week 6 isn’t the ideal time to tweak your special teams, but it happens, and the Rams either overcome it or they don’t.

Even if L.A. doesn’t fix its third unit for the 2026 season, they have to keep trying for their future. So, like the moves or not, the Rams are trying out some things, and that’s what they’ll have to keep doing until the get it right, if they get it right. Keep trying.

The Rams have been trying to fix or improve their special teams on a consistent level for a while now. It’s a massive storyline that likely won’t be going away anytime until the issues are fixed. If the issues are fixed.

Rams Make Flurry of Roster Moves as Kicker Blake Grupe Headlines Three Additions (sports.yahoo)

“Additionally, the Rams signed cornerback Damarion Williams to give them some depth on the practice squad. Williams was a fourth-round pick by the Baltimore Ravens in 2022. Given Jaylen Watson’s injuries, the Rams need some cornerback depth. Williams spent time with the Seahawks in 2024 and has also been with the Buccaneers over the last two years.

Williams is a smaller cornerback at 5-foot-10 and 180 pounds, with arms measuring less than 30 inches. However, he may bring some special teams value. He played 134 special teams snaps in 2022 as a rookie, but has not played much since.“

Jets’ Special Teams Unit Takes a Turn Thanks to Rams (sports.yahoo)

“The Los Angeles Rams, the team many predicted to win the Super Bowl after acquiring Myles Garrett in the offseason, have signed Blake Grupe off the Jets’ practice squad this week after a struggling start to the season from Ex-Jet Harrison Mevis.

You read that right. Los Angeles is going back to the Jets to solve its kicking problems.

The jokes write themselves.

Rams turn to Jets for help

Before he was cut on Tuesday, Mevis was easily the weakest link to the Rams roster. He went 5-9 on field goals including missing a potential game-winner on Monday night. Grupe, meanwhile, hasn’t even attempted a kick for the Jets so far this season.“

Bradley Chubb Addresses Postgame Altercation After Defeating The Los Angeles Rams (buffalobills.com)

“Watch Bills outside linebacker Bradley Chubb speak following the Buffalo Bills practice at UC Irvine in Newport Beach, California on October 14, 2026.”

Rams’ Alaric Jackson has suspension reduced to one game (sports.yahoo)

“Jackson appealed the suspension.

“Hearing officer Derrick Brooks, jointly appointed by the NFL and the NFLPA, has reduced the two game suspension of Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson to one game,” Michael Signora, the NFL’s senior vice president of football and international communications, said on social media.

Jackson must sit out Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals but is eligible to return for an Oct. 25 game against the Las Vegas Raiders.“

Cardinals vs. Rams Week 6 Preview | NFL Daily (nfl.com)

“Gregg Rosenthal and Jourdan Rodrigue preview the Week 6 matchup between the Cardinals and the Rams.”

Rams Injury Report Brings Much-Needed Good News Ahead of Week 6 vs. Cardinals (si.com)

“The Los Angeles Rams are set to enter Week 6 the healthiest they’ve been in weeks ahead of their matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. While the Rams didn’t practice on Wednesday, each player’s status is an estimation. On the injury report Rams had only one player who was estimated to not participate. That player was tight end Davis Allen, who would have missed practice with a foot injury. Outside of Allen, the Rams only had five other players listed, with four of them limited.“ 

NFL QB rankings, Week 6: Josh Allen reclaims No. 1 spot; Jordan Love makes biggest jump (nfl.com)

“Josh Allen played his purest form of football on Monday night, accepting the passing game might not be his best avenue toward victory and instead using his legs to rack up 121 rushing yards. He’s one of very few quarterbacks who carries elite value as a rusher and truly forces defenses to defend every play twice. It made for a nightmare for Los Angeles’ defense Monday. 

It wasn’t a scintillating Sunday for Bock Purdy, who was made uncomfortable by Seattle’s defense. But what Purdy did amid the challenges only reinforced his position atop the Index. His touchdown pass to Brandin Cooks and ensuing two-point conversion were fantastic examples of his never-quit playstyle that, to this point, hasn’t hurt him much.

Jared Goff is quietly putting together a stellar season, torching Arizona with ease while pushing his TD-INT ratio to a perfect 12-0.

Next Gen Stats insight (via NFL Pro): Josh Allen rushed for 107 yards on scrambles in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams, the most by any player this season and third-most in a game in the Next Gen Stats era. Since 2016, Allen has rushed for 100+ yards on scrambles twice, while the entire rest of the NFL has also done so just twice.“

3 lessons Rams can learn from Cardinals’ loss to Lions last week (ramswire)

“Here are three lessons from that contest the Rams can take into this week.

“The tight ends will always be open if the offense is patient
The Lions dismantled the Cardinals, and the Rams should do the same on offense. Arizona does not have enough talent on defense to keep up, and its only chance is if it’s able to take advantage of Alaric Jackson being suspended. To combat this, the Rams should give David Quessenberry some help while moving the pocket to the right periodically.“

Matthew Stafford and the Rams smell blood in the water against a Cardinals defense in free fall (nypost)

“Less than a week after a shocking 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills that bordered on criminal negligence, Sean McVay and the Rams (2-3) return to the house that Stan Kroenke built looking to salvage their season against a Cardinals (1-4) team that has lost four straight games.

For the Cardinals, another loss might have fans dreaming at night about Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith and the upcoming 2027 NFL Draft. 

For the Rams, another defeat and it’s time to sound the alarm on a season that once had such high Super Bowl aspirations before it began. “

Tyler Higbee is having an emphatic renaissance in Year 11 with the Rams (ramblinfan)

“As measured by per-game averages, Higbee was sneakily the Rams’ most productive tight end last season. Sidelined by an ankle injury, Higbee played only 10 games but produced 25 catches for 281 yards and three touchdowns. That pace would have led the room in receiving yards over Parkinson, the actual leader with 408, had Higbee stayed healthy.

And he did that while managing residual discomfort in his knee from Joseph’s years-old cheap shot. It’s not just his statistical production in 2026. Higbee is moving fluidly. He looks athletic. Almost young. 

The longest-tenured Ram – call it a tie with defensive lineman Aaron Donald, who’s also in his 11th season with the team after a two-year absence – Higbee has four seasons of at least 500 receiving yards. He would have had another in 2023, when he closed at 495, had he not missed two games.“

Comment of the Day:

“3 college kickers coming out this year with Greg Zeurlein leg strength…
Tate Sandell Oklahoma (he’s the one I’d draft)
Peyton Woodring Georgia
Lucas Carniero Ole Miss

Kicker, linebacker (with speed and size), and WR are the Rams biggest needs. Whether McVay sees it that way is another matter.“ -JeffinBranson

item.title: A bigger challenge awaits Packers’ secondary on Sunday night
item.description: The Packers’ defense will have their hands full with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.
item.content:encoded:
The Green Bay Packers’ defense had a marvelous performance in Week 5. The unit recorded nearly as many turnovers (five) as they allowed points in a 31-7 victory over the Chicago Bears. That team, which cycled through backup quarterbacks Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum, had put up 375 yards or more in its two games without Caleb Williams coming in, but they couldn’t cross the 250-yard mark against Green Bay.

This week, however, the Packers should have a tougher challenge on their hands. Chicago’s offense centers on the run game, but the Dallas Cowboys, who come into Lambeau Field for Sunday Night Football, have been doing their work through the air. Dallas has one of the most efficient offense in football on a per-drive basis to this point in the season, and most of that is due to a passing game that features a top wideout tandem of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.

The Packers have their own ascending receiver pairing, and although the Dallas duo are certainly more established, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden should have plenty of opportunities against a Dallas defense that ranks 31st in yards per pass attempt allowed. But on the other side of the ball Green Bay needs to find a way to limit Lamb and Pickens defensively. Lamb did not play in last year’s 40-40 tie at AT&T Stadium, but Pickens caught 8 passes for 134 yards and two scores.

Injuries could impact the Packers’ secondary this week as well, so let’s take a look at that as we slowly make our way towards Sunday Night Football.

Packers ‘can’t shy away’ from Cowboys’ explosive offense | Packers.com
Dallas is 7th in the NFL in scoring, 3rd in points per drive, and first in yards per drive and plays per drive. It’s going to be a challenge for Green Bay’s defense to get off the field without giving up points.

Packers safety Xavier McKinney back to hunting interceptions | Packersnews.com ($)
On the encouraging side, McKinney had a huge game last Sunday and looks rejuvenated after a bit of a down 2025 season.

Packers CB Keisean Nixon misses practice ahead of matchup with Cowboys WR duo | Packers Wire
Not encouraging is two of the Packers’ cornerbacks missing practice (Nixon and Benjamin St-Juste).

We Asked About Play-Action Passing; Packers Provided Explosive Answer | SI.com
The Packers did identify an advantage with play-action against the Bears, however, as Jordan Love went 12-for-13 for 245 yards and a score.

Micah Parsons wants to ensure ‘all the small things fixed first’ before return | ESPN
It sounds like the big concern now before he can return is making sure that everything is balanced and he won’t be overcompensating for the recovering ACL with different muscles. That said, if it were playoff time, he said he’d be playing, so he’s hopefully getting close.

What do you think? Is the Cowboys’ terrible defense bad enough to let this running game finally get on track?

item.title: Our Offense vs. Their Defense: New York Giants
item.description: Saints offense will have to be ready for another aggressive defense when they take one the Giants this Sunday
item.content:encoded:
The New Orleans Saints are traveling to New York/New Jersey to take on the Giants. The Giants are actually doing very well under first-year head coach Jim Harbaugh, especially considering they lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart for the season. The Giants are 3-1-1 on the year right now and are feeling very confident.

The Giants’ defense is led by Dennard Wilson, who was with the Titans last season. The Saints struggled against the Vikings’ heavy-pressure defense, and Wilson and the Giants will bring a lot of the same. The two most blitz-heavy defenses last week were the Vikings and Giants, respectively.

The Giants are not as formidable as the Vikings, but they are still a very good defense nonetheless. Currently, they rank 15th in total defense and seventh in passing defense. The advantage the Saints would like to exploit would be against their run defense, which ranks 25th in the league.

They are also a top-10 scoring defense, allowing only 21.2 points per game. They rank third in the league in interceptions with six and have eight total takeaways on the season.

The Saints’ offense does not match up too well against this defense. The struggles they experienced last week in the Dome could very well plague them again on the road.

The best way for the Saints to attack this team would be through the running game, but that’s something the Saints have yet to figure out how to do consistently.

New Orleans will have to find a way to get the offense into third-and-manageable situations. The Giants rank 27th in the league in third-down defense, and if the Saints can find a way to stay ahead of the chains, they could potentially find themselves in the red zone.

If they make it into the red zone, this is another area where the Giants’ defense struggles. They allow touchdowns on 69.2% of opponents’ red-zone possessions.

Third-down and red-zone conversions are actually strengths for this Saints offense, as they currently rank sixth in third-down conversion rate and third in red-zone touchdown conversion rate.

The problem is that they are either giving the ball away or putting themselves behind the chains with pre-snap penalties and poor execution in the running game.

The Saints have a chance, but which Saints team will travel to New York? Will it be the team that went to Baltimore and upset the Ravens for their lone win of the season, or the team that embarrassed themselves against the Falcons?

item.title: How former Cyclones performed in Week 5 of the NFL
item.description: Eleven former Cyclones made appearances in Week 5 of the NFL and played a combined 416 snaps on offense, defense and special teams. Breece Hall – New York Jets Hall did not play against the Cleveland Browns due to a quad injury sustained during the Lions game in week three. Jake Hummel – Houston Texans Hummel […]
item.content:encoded:
Eleven former Cyclones made appearances in Week 5 of the NFL and played a combined 416 snaps on offense, defense and special teams.

Breece Hall – New York Jets

Hall did not play against the Cleveland Browns due to a quad injury sustained during the Lions game in week three.

Jake Hummel – Houston Texans

Hummel was placed on injured reserve on Sept. 26.

Xavier Hutchinson – Houston Texans

In a 26-3 win against the Tennessee Titans, Hutchinson started and recorded four receptions for 65 yards. He appeared on the field for 27 offensive snaps.

Charlie Kolar – Los Angeles Chargers

In a 23-17 loss to the Denver Broncos, Kolar started and recorded three receptions for 37 yards. He played 51 snaps on offense and six on special teams.

Will McDonald IV – New York Jets

In a 17-12 win against the Browns, McDonald did start. He recorded two tackles and a strip sack in which he recovered Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson’s fumble. McDonald played 29 defensive snaps and 15 on special teams.

David Montgomery – Houston Texans

In a 26-3 win against the Titans, Montgomery started. He tallied 11 yards rushing on five carries. Montgomery recorded nine offensive snaps and sustained a groin injury. He is considered “week-to-week”.

Kene Nwangwu – New York Jets

In a 17-12 win against the Browns, Nwangwu did not start. but he did return three kickoffs by Andre Szmyt for a total of 68 yards. He recorded four snaps, all on special teams.

Jaylin Noel – Houston Texans

In a 26-3 win over the Titans, Noel did not start. He tallied five receptions for 41 yards, one rush for one yard, returned two punts for 21 yards, returned one kickoffs for 22 yards and a pancake block. Noel recorded 30 offensive snaps and eight on special teams.

Domonique Orange – Minnesota Vikings

In a 23-13 win against New Orleans, Orange did not start. He played five defensive snaps and two on special teams.

Darien Porter – Las Vegas Raiders

In a 45-17 loss against the New England Patriots, Darien Porter did not start, but recorded seven tackles, defended two passes and recovered a fumble. He played 50 defensive snaps and 14 on special teams.

Brock Purdy – San Francisco 49ers

In an 32-29 win against the Seahawks, Purdy went 19-of-29 through the air for 189 yards and two touchdowns, with his longest pass going 28 yards to Mike Evans. He also had five carries for six yards and played all 60 offensive snaps.

TJ Tampa – Baltimore Ravens

Tampa has been on injured reserve since Sept. 19.

Jalen Travis – Indianapolis Colts

In a 34-22 loss against the Pittsburgh Steelers, Travis started at right tackle and played 67 offensive snaps and six special teams snaps.

Eyioma Uwazurike – Denver Broncos

In a 23-17 win over the Chargers, Uwazurike started on the defensive line. He recorded four tackles and played 30 defensive snaps as well as three special teams snaps.

item.title: Cowboys point/counterpoint: The embarrassment of being in the NFC East
item.description: The NFC East is a tough scene.
item.content:encoded:
Well, at least the Dallas Cowboys are not alone in their misery. The Philadelphia Eagles let the Jacksonville Jaguars steal a game from them in London, then the New York Giants and Washington Commanders put on an amazing display of ineptitude at the end of their overtime tie.

First, the Giants handed the Commanders a golden opportunity to kick the winning field goal. Then, with time running out, Jayden Daniels apparently forgot they were out of time outs and let the clock run down to zero with his team in range for what should have been an easy field goal.

That hardly makes us feel better. But it does bring up the question asked here, and heard from the announcers of the Giants-Commanders game: Does anyone want to win the NFC East?

Sean – After all the dust settled on this comical, disastrous week for the NFC East, I had the following thought – which team actually benefits the most from winning the division, if it stays the way it’s going and continues to look like the winner won’t be a real threat in the playoffs?

The Giants have the longest playoff drought, but also a season-ending injury to their starting QB. The Eagles in some ways appear to be making a statement that just winning this lousy division isn’t good enough, if they aren’t true Super Bowl contenders they rather build for a future where they are. The Dan Quinn experiment in Washington feels like it’s all but over, but a playoff berth could see him stay. 

I really think the answer is our team, Tom. Coach Schottenheimer’s predecessor was let go because he couldn’t advance in the playoffs, but at least he proved consistently he could get there. We don’t even know if Schotty can guide the team to the postseason yet, and it still doesn’t feel like any team around the NFC at large is “unbeatable”. 

In order for the Cowboys to turn this around and actually grab the NFC East’s low-hanging fruit of a playoff spot, and do so with any conviction, they’re going to have to fix a lot of defensive issues against the Packers. Matt LaFleur is going to be licking his chops seeing the Cowboys defensive tape from the Bucs game, doing so fresh off a win against the hated Chicago Bears too. 

There’s been a lot of talk in recent weeks about desperate teams, desperate coaching staffs, and on and on. I don’t exactly have a lot of faith in the Cowboys staff, one that added Mike Pettine on Monday, to really embrace this mantra and be as prepared for the Packers as they need to be.

Tom – It is hard not to cringe about what is likely going to face the Cowboys in the storied confines of Lambeau Field. Jordan Love went off on the Chicago Bears. We are all well aware of just how woefully vulnerable the Dallas defense has been this season.

Yet this game has the potential for the Cowboys to get right. I’m not saying it’s a big potential, but it still exists. The Packers are an even more one-dimensional offense than Dallas, ranking dead last in rushing yards per game. One possible way for the visitors to eke out a win is to play ball control offense and keep Love on the bench for long stretches, while scoring consistently on their own possessions.

That may be a tall order, however. Dallas is barely ahead of Green Bay in running the ball. The Packers have a clear edge in both points allowed and sacks. And Dak Prescott has to have a much better game than he did against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. As good as he can be some times, Prescott also can have games where he is just off. That seemed to be the case in their latest loss. We have to hope he has a bounce back when they head north.

Maybe the real question is not who wants to win the NFC East. It might be who has the ability. None of the teams in the division have demonstrated that so far. Whoever manages to do so could make the playoffs to represent the NFCE. Now we have to see if the Cowboys have that in them.

Sean – My hope for this game is that Love’s deep ball performance against a Bears defense that was suspect to such throws last year as well can be a bit of an outlier, but man the Cowboys cornerback and safety play shouldn’t make anyone feel great about winning this differential. The Cowboys may not have to, if they really do stick with the run game and play a little bit more ball control like you said. 

All that said, I’m not sure why I still feel as optimistic as I do about this team. I am far from the level of doom and gloom that’s coming out of the Bucs loss, but we said a bit of the same after the Ravens loss too so maybe I’m just staying aboard the same ship. 

The defense needs to get healthier before we can fully assess how much they will help this team going forward. The offense is a different story, they need to come out looking pissed off about what happened to them last Thursday night in this game.

When it comes to that ability to win the NFC East you mentioned Tom, the difference maker feels obvious to me. Whichever team can string together a win streak of any significance. The Cowboys don’t have back to back wins since last November, and that is certainly bad.

The Eagles only back-to-back wins this year are against the Commanders and Titans, though. The Giants also beat the Titans then the Cardinals back to back. The Commanders have the most impressive single win of anyone in the division by beating the defending Super Bowl champs with a backup QB, but no win streak to speak of.

The time is definitely right here and now for the Cowboys to get two wins against the Packers and Eagles to change the mood of the season the best they can.

Tom – One thing that has been worrying me lately is the spreading opinion that the Dallas players are just kind of giving up on too many plays. There just doesn’t seem to be much of that dog in them that winning teams exhibit.

I think that has to be laid at the feet of the coaching staff. They need to light a fire under this team. It may be time to bench a starter or two to push the rest of the roster. I would suggest that DaRon Bland and Jake Ferguson have both had too many errors of late and would be prime candidates for at least a temporary demotion. It may seem a drastic move, but this team needs to do something drastic. 

And the recent hire of Mike Pettine could be seen as just such a move, which would make some roster shakeup logical. 

Despite a couple of really bad games this season, Dallas is still in contention for the division title thanks to some similarly bad games played by the rest of the NFC East. Bouncing back and getting a win on the road in Green Bay could get this team back on track.

But if they lay another egg, they risk letting a golden opportunity to get back to the playoffs slip through their grasp just like the football has been doing far too often of late.

Sean – Coach Schotty has already teased that there will be personnel changes going into this game, so in this case we’ll have to “wait all day for Sunday night” to really keep a close eye on the lineups. Brew some extra coffee before kickoff. This might be a bit too far outside the box, but I’m wondering out loud if the Pettine hire can lead to more of James Houston at linebacker/pass rush. 

I agree with you completely on Ferguson. The Cowboys best offensive plays against the Bucs (and there weren’t nearly enough of them) came when they had extra blockers in against the blitz, let Prescott stand in there, and fire the ball to either CeeDee Lamb or more often than not, George Pickens.

The idea of Ferguson being the third seam-stretching element to this offense is enticing, I get it. But he wasn’t even contributing to that blocking, it was mostly Javonte Williams at the RB spot. Keep it simple and rely as much as you possibly can on Pickens, Lamb, and Ryan Flournoy. That trio is good enough to win with on offense, I really believe that.

Clearly getting too high off a win is something this team is still struggling with, but now they’re in a position of having to hope that applies to the Packers who just beat the Bears for the first time in three tries. The Cowboys need a tight performance in all three phases with extra rest to expect this from them at Lambeau. 

As always, good chatting with you Tom. The Bobcats are off their bye and back in action this Saturday so it will be a football-filled weekend for me complete with staying up late on Sunday night. Let’s have more fun than last Thursday.

item.title: Week 6 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Cowboys and Packers had much different results last week
item.description: The Packers rebounded in a big way last week, while the Cowboys fell apart.
item.content:encoded:
One week can change the entire perception of an NFL team. Sometimes that's good, sometimes it's not.

The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers were both 2-2 coming into last week's games. The Cowboys weren't considered a Super Bowl contender, but they were at least looking OK — especially in a bad NFC East — with a home game against the winless Buccaneers coming up. The Packers had played so poorly through four weeks that they were home underdogs to the Bears for the first time in 20 years, even though Chicago had its backup quarterback.

The Cowboys and Packers come into Week 6's Sunday night game with their seasons flipped around.

The Cowboys looked horrible against the Buccaneers, losing to an undrafted rookie quarterback. The defensive problems finally got to a point in which the Cowboys hired longtime NFL defensive coordinator Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant and said defensive coordinator Christian Parker will now call plays from the press box. There's always some angst in Dallas because of the attention on the Cowboys all the time, but it's not like the defensive problems are made up. Dallas was 32nd in defensive DVOA last season and they're 32nd so far this season.

Meanwhile, the talk of Matt LaFleur being on the hot seat seems like it was a lot longer than a week ago. The best way to gain back the confidence of Packers fans is to blow out the Bears, and the Packers did that. They blasted Chicago 31-7, with Jordan Love embarrassing the Bears defense with his deep passing and Green Bay shutting down everything Chicago's offense wanted to do. After not playing a good game through four weeks, the Packers played a great game in Week 5.

That makes Week 6 hard to figure out. Do the Cowboys rebound or is the defense simply unfixable? What's the real Packers team, the one that couldn't run the ball, couldn't protect Love and had a below-average defense through four games, or the one we saw Sunday?

The Packers are a small favorite on Sunday night, indicating the oddsmakers don't have a lot of confidence in them still. But it's tougher to bank on the Cowboys' defense. Packers -1.5 is the pick, though it could all look different for both teams next week. That's how the NFL goes.

Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 6 of the NFL season:

Seahawks (-2.5) over Broncos

Not all is great for the Seahawks, who can't run the ball and still don't have an offensive option other than Jaxon Smith-Njigba. But they've been far better than the Broncos, who were on their way to losing to the winless and injury-plagued Chargers before saving themselves with a fourth-quarter rally. The matchup of Seattle's defense against an aimless Broncos offense is enough to take Denver.

Jaguars (-2.5) over Texans

A bit of a weird line. The Jaguars are 4-1 and while last week's miracle win over the Eagles wasn't great, they do look like a legitimate contender in the AFC. The Texans are 1-4 and their win came against the 0-5 Titans. And yet, in a neutral site game — if either team has the edge it's Jacksonville, who does the London trip every season and stayed overseas after playing there last week — the Jaguars aren't even giving a full field goal. Yes it's a desperate Houston team with a very good defense. But it's not a lot of respect for the Jaguars.

Falcons (+1.5) over Bears

It appears Michael Penix Jr. and Caleb Williams will start, which should make for an entertaining game. The big question for this one will be what to make of the Bears defense. In Week 1 and 5 they gave up 68 points. From Weeks 2-4 they allowed 28 points. The hot stretch in the middle could have come from facing three bad offenses (Vikings without Kyler Murray, Eagles, Jets) instead of the Panthers and Packers, their other two opponents who both got more than 30 points. The Falcons are a good offense with Penix, so points should be coming.

Browns (+5.5) over Ravens

The Ravens should have confidence after beating the Falcons without Lamar Jackson last week. But a Tyler Huntley offense still isn't one I'm comfortable laying 5.5 points on the road with.

Buccaneers (+2.5) over Steelers

Metrics like DVOA and net EPA per play says these teams are practically even. The Buccaneers have the rest advantage, having played last Thursday night, and the Steelers are 0-2 on the road (3-0 at home). Rookie Jalon Daniels could be exposed by the best defense who he has faced, but it's also not the intimidating Steelers defense from recent years.

Patriots (-7.5) over Jets

The Patriots are officially warmed up. The start to the season was lackluster but Drake Maye is coming off two good games in a row. The Jets are better than some expected, but they're facing a team that has its season back on track and wants to keep that going.

Giants (+1.5) over Saints

It's hard to buy the Giants. There's no evidence they're a good team despite their 3-1-1 record. But it's not like there are any signs that the Saints are much better. New Orleans is 30th in DVOA ahead of only the hopeless Titans and Dolphins. Anything can happen when Jameis Winston is starting at quarterback, good or bad. Good luck predicting it.

Panthers (-1) over Eagles

It's weird to see the Panthers favored at Philadelphia (though some books have the Eagles as a small favorite). But to this point, Carolina has been the far better team. Also, they're coming off a bye while the Eagles come right off a flight from London, where they took a horrific loss after kicking a go-ahead field goal with eight seconds left.

Colts (-7) over Titans

The TItans should be very happy the Dolphins exist this season, or else there would be even more talk about how bad they are. Indianapolis hasn't been great either but it's just too difficult to take the Titans right now.

Cardinals (+12.5) over Rams

It's quite possible the Rams take out their frustrations on the Cardinals. The Rams are 2-3, but the schedule has been tough and it starts to ease up with a game against the Cardinals, who just got throttled by the Lions. Arizona seems to be running out of steam after looking decent to start the season. Still, 12.5 points is a lot considering the Rams haven't looked great yet and the Cardinals can move the ball, especially in garbage time.

Raiders (+5.5) over Bills

The Bills are coming off an emotional, difficult overtime win against the Rams on Monday night. They are the better team but that's a tough situational spot and the Raiders are not as bad as they looked last week against the Patriots. Let's give the Raiders one more shot to show that 3-0 start wasn't fraudulent.

Chiefs (-8) over Chargers

The Chargers aren't just bad, they're injured. They held their own against the Broncos last week but that probably says more about Denver. This season is already ugly for the Chargers and it's not going to get much better.

Commanders (+7.5) over 49ers

If the Commanders aren't completely downtrodden after one of the dumbest endings in recent NFL history last week, in which they casually watched the final minute of overtime run out without getting a field-goal attempt, then this seems like too many points. The 49ers have played very well on both sides of the ball (the defense has been a great surprise), but there is some danger of a letdown after winning at Seattle. Take the points and hope last week's fiasco doesn't still linger for Washington.

item.title: Value of Things: By the Numbers
item.description: Is the Texans defense a part of the problem this year?
item.content:encoded:
Last week we did some internal scouting on the Texans offense. This week we shift our attention to the defense. As we do with most things, we break down the overall numbers into their individual parts. The key to the Texans defense has always been two-fold. You shut down the opponents running game and then make the opposing quarterbacks day miserable. The Texans have been particularly good under DeMeco Ryans on the last part of that statement.

Instead of doing totals it is usually better to look at these things game by game. When you have only five games on the schedule you can have one or two games that skew results one way or another. Only the 2000 Baltimore Ravens and 1985 Chicago Bears have been dominant enough to dominate all of their opponents. For most teams we are looking at a preponderance of the evidence. So, let’s start with the game by game running defense results.

Rushing Defense

So, when you look at it this way you would have to say that the Texans defense is as good as it has always been against the run. Furthermore, they have been getting steadily better since the Buffalo game. That makes perfect sense since Josh Allen is one of the better running quarterbacks in the NFL. Additionally, the Texans have been getting healthier as they got Kayden McDonald back in the defensive tackle rotation. They also got Alzeez Al-Shaair back as well.

The big key are the attempts. The opponents are not even trying to run the ball anymore. This is even though every game except for the Titans game has either been competitive or opponents have been playing ahead. That should tell us something. It tells us one of two things. Either teams are giving up on the run because it has been ineffective or because the pass has become more effective.

Again, we can look at totals and that could tell us a lot, but I would prefer to look at the quarterbacks and how successful they have been. The Texans defense has famously made some really good quarterbacks look really awful on the season. The good news is that three of the first four quarterbacks are generally regarded as top ten quarterbacks in the NFL. However, the numbers might tell us something else.

Passing Defense

So, this is a glass half empty and half full deal. The three elite quarterbacks played like elite quarterbacks. The two that aren’t didn’t. So, the good news is that we aren’t making bad or average quarterbacks look good. We just aren’t making any of the good ones look bad. Obviously, what this means for the future depends on where you would peg Trevor Lawrence and the quarterbacks that follow.

To put it another way, we are looking at C.J. Stroud as having his best season since his rookie year. How would we feel about his performance if these were his games? For one, his completion percentage would be higher than it is now, but he would have fewer yards. The six touchdowns and two interceptions would be slightly worse overall than what he is currently producing. The aggregate pass rating is almost exactly what Stroud is putting up at 96.3.

Those are the numbers. The whys and what fors are generally more difficult to pinpoint. For one, it is clear that Kamari Lassiter is not having the same kind of season he had last year. Is it a blip on the radar or have other teams figured him out? Secondly, Reed Blankenship obviously struggled in his first few games as a Texan. Again, is this is a situation of him feeling out his place in the defense or was his signing a mistake? These are all important questions moving forward.

DeMeco Ryans taking back the playcalling is only in its first week. We honestly don’t know if this last week was an uptick or just the Titans being the Titans. One thing is also true. This team hasn’t generated turnovers like they did last season. That could be blind luck or a sign that they are not as good. Either is equally likely at this point and probably both are true in some respects. One thing is for certain, if defenses keep carving up the Texans in the passing game then they will have to try different coverages, blitz packages, and other wrinkles because simply being better than everyone else is not working this year like it has in seasons past.

item.title: NFL Week 6 Survivor/Eliminator Picks
item.description: By the start of Week 6 last year, we had no undefeated teams left, one winless team. In 2024, two undefeated and one winless. 2023, two and one. 2022, one and zero. This year, we have three of each. The…
item.content:encoded:
By the start of Week 6 last year, we had no undefeated teams left, one winless team. In 2024, two undefeated and one winless. 2023, two and one. 2022, one and zero. This year, we have three of each. The Chiefs, Vikings and 49ers have yet to lose; the Chargers, Titans and Dolphins have yet to win. In several ways, that makes our job easier — pick one of the undefeated teams, or pick someone facing one of the winless teams. If you can find someone that fits both those classifications, even better! (Spoiler alert?) Let’s see how that plays out. Check out my Week 6 pick for Survivor contests. And while we’re here, you can use our NFL Betting Model and our Bet Tracker to make a pick for yourself.

NFL Survivor Picks for Week 6

Every week, we have the same process. We eliminate teams in groups until we narrow it down to our real considerations. Start with all 32, whittle it down. And remember — this game is “once you use a team, they’re off the board,” so it’s not always just a matter of taking the team you think will win. There has to be some strategy. I can’t pick a team I’ve picked before, but you might not have tailed me, so previously used teams are eligible until the end.

Bye Weeks

My favorite category — picks I can’t get wrong! If you don’t play, you can’t win, but also I won’t pick you, so woohoo for easy. Cincinnati Bengals Detroit Lions Miami Dolphins Minnesota Vikings That’s four off the board.

Opponent Is Too Good

Maybe these are good teams, maybe not, but it’s too hard to trust them given who they are facing. This is a 10-team list every week (fewer when there are byes); we are eliminating anyone facing a top-10 team in our FTN NFL Power Rankings. Arizona Cardinals (@ LA Rams) Cleveland Browns (vs. Baltimore) Denver Broncos (vs. Seattle) Houston Texans (vs. Jacksonville in London) Las Vegas Raiders (vs. Buffalo) Los Angeles Chargers (@ Kansas City) Seattle Seahawks (@ Denver) Washington Commanders (@ San Francisco) Some of these teams will win but you can’t confidently say so, considering who they’re facing. That’s eight more gone, 20 to go.

They’re Too Bad

You can face the worst team in all of football, but if you’re the second-worst team, well, I’m still not going to be too excited about selecting you. We’ll return to the power rankings here and cross off any team in the bottom 12. Indianapolis Colts (vs. Tennessee) New Orleans Saints (@ NY Giants) New York Giants (vs. New Orleans) New York Jets (@ New England) Philadelphia Eagles (vs. Carolina) Tampa Bay Buccaneers (vs. Pittsburgh) Tennessee Titans (@ Indianapolis) Seven more eliminations leaves us with 13 remaining.

Island Games

Island games just get weird. I would need some very convincing evidence to pick anyone on a Thursday, or a Monday, or an overseas 9:30 a.m. ET game. There aren’t many left this week, but I still want to note them. Dallas Cowboys (@ Green Bay) Green Bay Packers (vs. Dallas) Jacksonville Jaguars (vs. Houston in London) San Francisco 49ers (vs. Washington) Four more gone, nine left — our nine contenders.

The Contenders

Once we’re down to this small a number of teams, we’re done cutting them in swaths. We look at the pros and cons for each team and then figure it out. I’m also diving into our NFL Betting Model to see what the numbers think of the game.

Atlanta Falcons (vs. Chicago)

Model Projection: Bears 24.20-23.99, Falcons 49.5% win rate Pros: If Michael Penix Jr. can play, this offense can feast against the Bears D. Cons: If Penix can’t go, it’s Tua Tagovailoa time, and that’s scary.

Baltimore Ravens (@ Cleveland)

Model Projection: Ravens 22.15-20.52, Ravens 54.8% win rate Pros: Even though they’re 3-2, no one is scared of the Browns. Cons: We’re either getting a slightly hobbled Lamar Jackson or a backup quarterback.

Buffalo Bills (@ Las Vegas)

Model Projection: Bills 31.77-22.95, Bills 69.3% win rate Pros: Josh Allen is maybe the most dangerous weapon in NFL history. Cons: Allen’s danger sometimes boomerangs back on the Bills, and it was just a couple weeks ago the Raiders were 3-0.

Carolina Panthers (@ Philadelphia)

Model Projection: Eagles 21.55-21.20, Eagles 51.0% win rate Pros: Bryce Young looks like he’s making the leap this year, and the Eagles are a mess. Cons: If you’d floated locking the Panthers against the Eagles even three weeks ago, you’d have gotten laughed out of the room.

Chicago Bears (@ Atlanta)

Model Projection: Bears 24.20-23.99, Bears 50.5% win rate Pros: Caleb Williams should return, and the Chicago offense could be back to normal if so. Cons: Hobbled Caleb Williams on one side, Bijan Robinson on the other?

Kansas City Chiefs (vs. LA Chargers)

Model Projection: Chiefs 25.71-18.64, Chiefs 69.1% win rate Pros: The Chiefs are one of the best teams in football and are coming off a bye. The Chargers super-duper-very are not. Cons: Want to save the Chiefs for later? Worried about the WR injuries? It’s hard to find many reasons.

Los Angeles Rams (vs. Arizona)

Model Projection: Rams 30.13-19.93, Rams 73.8% win rate Pros: The Rams are playing angry, but even if not, they are several classes above the Cardinals. Cons: Maybe the Rams just aren’t as good as we thought?

New England Patriots (vs. NY Jets)

Model Projection: Patriots 26.47-17.57, Patriots 73.6% win rate Pros: Drake Maye has gotten back to normal the last couple weeks, meaning the Pats again have elite upside. Cons: It was just two weeks ago that people were jumping off the Maye ship en masse.

Pittsburgh Steelers (@ Tampa Bay)

Model Projection: Steelers 26.37-19.67, Steelers 67.5% win rate Pros: Aaron Rodgers is playing his best football since his Green Bay days. Cons: The Bucs got in the win column last week and get to play host here.

The Pick

Kansas City Chiefs (vs. LA Chargers)

I don’t love that Tyquan Thornton is out, or that Rashee Rice likely is as well. But that’s a small concern in an otherwise should-be-flawless situation. The Chiefs are regularly good out of the bye, Patrick Mahomes is playing great, Kenneth Walker III looks like a possible Offensive Player of the Year, the Chiefs are at home. The Chargers are a mess in every conceivable way, and the conversation around them is more about who might lose their job and when than it is about winning games. Easy pick.

Honorable Mention

Baltimore Ravens (@ Cleveland) Buffalo Bills (@ Las Vegas) 2026 record: 3-2 Week 1: Chargers (L) Week 2: Eagles (W) Week 3: Seahawks (L) Week 4: Vikings (W) Week 5: Bengals (W) Week 6: Chiefs

item.title: Opponent Breakdown: Syracuse Orange Defense
item.description: Fran Brown lost his defensive coordinator this offseason, but he arguably made an upgrade when he brought in Vince Kehres from Toledo. Kerhes led an outstanding group during his time at Toledo, and he did a very good job mining talent for a school that wasn’t playing big-time football. The Cuse defense looks improved early […]
item.content:encoded:
Fran Brown lost his defensive coordinator this offseason, but he arguably made an upgrade when he brought in Vince Kehres from Toledo. Kerhes led an outstanding group during his time at Toledo, and he did a very good job mining talent for a school that wasn’t playing big-time football. The Cuse defense looks improved early on this season, but the competition they have faced has not been exceptional. This group will have to step it up against a powerful Louisville offense.

The Cuse defense has gotten nice production from their edge defenders up front. Keyshawn Johnson and Tunmise Adeleye have combined for 7 tackles for loss and sacks this year, while combining for 29 total pressures. They combine with Nissi Ogbebor at defensive tackle to put a lot of pressure on the quarterback while also being solid against the run. Rashard Berry rounds out this group with his 4 tackles for loss to go along with one of the better big-man interceptions of the season.

Linebacker is the strength of the defense with two players who make up one of the best duos in the ACC. Chris D’Appolonia and Antoine Deslauriers have been very good for the Orange, racking up tackles and tackles for loss through the first half of the season. D’Appolonia was a nice addition for this defense as he followed Kerhes from Toledo after a very good season. Deslauriers was one of the best freshmen linebackers in the country last year, and he has picked up where he left off. These two will have their hands full if Louisville can continue to run the ball as they have over the last two weeks.

Syracuse has one of the best pass defenses in the country, with top 15 rankings in completion percentage and yards per attempt. They make teams work to complete passes, and they do a good job of keeping things in front of them to avoid big plays. Cuse has only allowed 30 passing plays for ten or more yards this year. That’s top-10 in the country and much better than a Wake Forest defense that put the clamps on Louisville’s explosive offense.

The individual players don’t stand out much for Cuse, but Davien Kerr flashes when you watch their games. The nickel corner has good speed and plays with the type of intensity you need as an interior defender. He has the lone interception by the secondary, and it came on a nice play where he jumped a route.

Chris Peal is second on the team in tackles from his safety spot, but he has been the one player that I have seen struggle in coverage this year. Peal has been beaten deep twice in man coverage down the field, while he was lined up in more of a cornerback alignment. It’s something to look out for on Saturday night, as the Cards will look for ways to push the ball down the field on the Orange.

item.title: Giants vs. Saints matchup: Can the Giants’ defense shut down the Saints’ offense?
item.description: What does the Giants defense need to do to disrupt the Saints’ offense?
item.content:encoded:
The New York Giants enter Week 6 as the leaders of the NFC East and return home after a Week 5 tie to face the New Orleans Saints.

This game marks the third time in three weeks that the Giants will underdogs to a last place team, as the 3-1-1 Giants are 1.5-point underdogs at home to the 1-4 Saints.

The Giants come into the game still looking to have their first complete performance since starting QB Jaxson Dart was lost for the season. the Giants are 2-0-1 since Dart was lost in Week 2, but have escaped losses by the skin of their teeth each time.

The Saints, meanwhile, are reeling after a 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings that saw the Vikings shut down the Saints’ offense. Can the Giants take lessons from the Vikings’ league-leading defense and get off to a fast start against New Orleans’ offense?

Stats that matter

What the Saints do on offense

When it comes to the passing game, Kellen Moore’s offensive philosophy has historically been a blend of the Air Coryell and West Coast schemes. He’s added modern twists and updates to those venerable schemes, but the foundation is the use of a West Coast quick game with Air Coryell style vertical concepts when opportunities present themselves.

They mix and match condensed and spread formations, while also asking Shough to work from under center as well as out of the shotgun. They typically use motion on nearly every play, as well as use bunch or stack sets to help secure clean releases for their receivers. The West Coast roots of the offense are evident in the structure of Moore’s passing play design. He frequently calls route concepts designed to create traffic or conflict at the second or third levels, and create receiving windows that his pass catchers can exploit.

Moore’s passing concepts frequently seem to feature half-field reads against the Minnesota Vikings, though that could be an attempt to counter the Vikings’ blitzing defense (more on that in a bit). Shough is capable of making full-field progression reads and the offense does ask him to do so, however half-field reads and quick-game passing concepts seem to be the bread and butter.

In that vein, there are instances where Shough can lock on to receivers or stare down spots from the snap, which could be an opportunity for the Giants’ opportunistic defense.

The Saints’ offense makes relatively frequent use of their tertiary receivers in the passing attack. Wide receiver turned tight end Juwan Johnson is Shough’s third-most targeted option, averaging just over 6 targets per game, while Alvin Kamara is fourth and averaging four targets per game. Both players serve as primary options in passing plays as well as check-down targets.

Moving to the running game, Kamara is the starter after Travis Etienne Jr. landed on the injured reserve after Week 3 with a hamstring injury. Kendre Miller is the change-up to Kamara as a power back, but both rnners have struggled to consistently produce. The 31-year old Kamara has averaged 3.1 yards per attempt this year, while Miller has averaged 2.9 per attempt.

But while Kamara was the starting running back, he only carried the ball three times against the Vikings. Miller, meanwhile, carried the ball 10 times.

Schematically, the Saints based their running game on outside zone concepts against the Vikings’ blitz schemes, however they did mix in gap schemes with pulling linemen. Both their line and Miller were more effective executing their outside zone runs.

Shough hunting

The Giants’ pass rush has been absolutely ferocious over the last two games. Abdul Carter might be the most fearsome pass rusher in the NFL right now, boasting an incredibly impressive 36% pass rush win rate despite being doubled on 40% of his rushes. His 2.22-second time to pressure is the fastest in the NFL, and he’s generating pressure — and quick pressures — at an elite rate. It isn’t a surprise that Carter also leads the NFL in pass rush wins with 31.

But while Carter is the player that that teams need to account for on every play, he isn’t carrying the by himself load both Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux generated three quick pressures apiece, while linebacker Arvell Reese, and defensive tackles D.J. Reader, and nDarius Alexander each contributed two quick pressures. Cornerback Dru Phillips led the team with five quick pressures (and two sacks) of Jayden Daniels.

The difference over the last two weeks has been the adjustment by Dennard Wilson to use the blitz to unleash the his pass rushers. Over the last two weeks, the Giants have sent five (or more) rushers 57% of the time, and 61% against the Washington Commanders.

The Giants’ blitz rate since the second quarter against the Arizona Cardinals is (distantly) second only to that of the Minnesota Vikings. I bring that up because the Vikings gave us a blueprint for how to attack Tyler Shough and the Saints’ offense.

The Vikings sent extra rushers on 21 of 25 drop backs against the Saints, limiting Shough to just 96 yards passing (3.8 per attempt), with 2 interceptions and 1 sack.

Pressuring Shough is an excellent way to disrupt the Saints’ passing offense. Shough is, generally, an efficient quarterback who’s a favorite of offensive coaches. He is generally faithful to the structure of the offense and play design and typically doesn’t put the ball in danger. He’s a good athlete who also has a live arm that allows him to access all areas of the field.

However, Shough is, in the words of former scout Nate Tice, “Very Tua-coded” as a passer. Shough takes care of the ball, but he’s also prone to throw the ball away as a first resort. He’s below league-average in interception rate, he’s also below league average in yards per attempt and touchdown rate. He also currently has the 10th-fastest time to throw of all quarterbacks, as he would rather get the ball out or throw it away than extend the play or hold the ball for a deep pass.

The pressure and difficult coverage reads created by the Vikings’ defense brought out Shough’s tendencies to throw the ball away rather than risk going backward or turn the ball over. That’s a tendency the Giants can, and should, look to exploit with their athleticism and aggression on defense.

There are, of course, differences in how Wilson and Flores deploy their blitz schemes. Flores has woven the blitz (or five-man rushes) into the very fabric and structure of every aspect of his defense. Everything is predicated on pressure under a two-deep shell, either true Quarters coverage or Cover-2. The goal of Flores’ scheme is to create free runs for his rushers while not allowing the offense to access the deep or intermediate area of the field. This is even true for his run defense, and the Vikings frequently use the blitz to “gap out” opposing offenses and disrupt their runs.

Wilson’s blitz schemes, meanwhile, are based on using sticky press-man coverage to take receivers away while his hyper-athletic linebackers do their thing. The Giants lead the league in Cover-0 usage, calling pure man coverage at a league-high 11%. To put that in perspective, Steve Spagnuolo and the Kansas City Chiefs led the NFL in Cover-0 usage last year at just 7.6%. That’s particularly impressive considering the Giants’ defensive adjustment is only seven quarters old.

While the Vikings’ defense has been much better than the Giants, the Giants have a marked advantage in athleticism at all three levels. That could allow them to severely disrupt what the Saints want to do on defense and harass (or attack) Shough.

However, the difference in structure presents two potential areas of concern against the Saints. The first is the presence of wide receiver Chris Olave. Olave was a lone bright spot for the Saints against the Vikings, and his precision route running gives man cover corners fits. He’s also a savvy veteran who knows how to manipulate defenders to expand receiving windows as well as get calls in his favor.

The other thing to note is that the Saints didn’t deploy screen plays against the Vikings defense. The screen is one of the most effective way to slow down a pass rush, however the pure zone coverage used by the Vikings limits how effective screens can be. On the flip side, screens can be very effective against man coverage, as the sticky nature of press-man coverage also leaves defenders close to blocking receivers and takes their eyes out of the backfield.

The Giants will need to be alert to screen plays to make sure the Saints aren’t able to turn their aggression against them with their athletic skill position players.

Can the Giants stop the run?

This is, of course, the question every week for the Giants. As head coach John Harbaugh mentioned after the Giants’ tie with the Commanders, the Giants have done a solid job of stopping the run — on occasion. However, they haven’t yet found any down-to-down consistency.

When the Giants have successfully defended the run, it’s been because their stout defensive tackles have clogged the middle while their athletic defenders have penetrated and disrupted behind the line of scrimmage. However, they’ve also had a tendency to commit mental mistakes — be it poor angles, missed tackles, or both — to give up explosive runs.

Teams have also been able to exploit their perimeter with well-schemed off-tackle runs that get big blockers (such as tight ends or linemen) pulling out to their corners. We should expect the Saints to try to exploit that tendency, as it not only plays into the relative strength of their running game and the weakness of the Giants’ defense.

As mentioned above, running back Kendre Miller carried the ball more than Alvin Kamara last week, though he only has one more carry on the season than Kamara. Miller is a downhill runner and was the hot hand against the Vikings, with carries of 9, 7, and 6 yards, as well as a touchdown. He’s a similar runner to Cam Skattebo and Najee Harris with good size (6-foot, 220 pounds) and burst, but modest long speed.

If the Saints turn to Miller, they’ll likely try to get him to the edge, pairing his size and burst against the Giants’ defensive backs. The Giants, meanwhile, will need to penetrate into the backfield and disrupt Miller before he can get going.

Kamara, meanwhile, depends on his vision and short-area quickness as a runner. He isn’t as explosive as he was in his prime, but he’s still elusive enough to make would-be tacklers miss if they take poor angles. The Saints like to take advantage of Kamara’s versatility and line him up as a receiver before motioning him into the backfield. That not only helps change the math in the tackle box, but also helps to reveal the defense’s intentions. Where the Giants will be well-served to penetrate and disrupt against Miller, defending Kamara is more a matter of discipline and rallying to the ball and limiting his room to work.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers on injuries at wide receiver: I have a lot of trust in our options
item.description: The Steelers are heading into Week 6 short on healthy wide receivers.
item.content:encoded:
The Steelers are heading into Week 6 short on healthy wide receivers.

Michael Pittman is on injured reserve and the team is set to be without Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek as well when they take the field in Tampa this Sunday. That leaves three wideouts on the active roster, although rookie Kaden Wetjen has yet to play an offensive snap yet this season.

The team has three more wideouts on the practice squad and quarterback Aaron Rodgers expressed his faith in Brandon Smith, Brandon Johnson, and Isaiah Hodgins while discussing the team's options on Wednesday.

"I have a lot of trust in those guys," Rodgers said, via the team's website. "I've always been a fan of Brandon Johnson; he had his locker right next to mine last year and we had some great conversations. He's played and played well when he's gotten opportunities. Obviously, I know B. Smith from New York and I'm a big believer in him. And then Isaiah was here with us last year, then went to New York and made a bunch of plays. I like those guys a lot."

The Steelers' ability to weather the injuries should be helped by how Rodgers uses all of the available targets. Running back Jaylen Warren and tight end Pat Freiermuth are tied with DK Metcalf for the team lead in catches while tight end Darnell Washington has also been used frequently in the passing game.
