item.title: Is it time to cut ties with Cardinals DC Nick Rallis?
item.description: The Lions game showed just how bad this defense can be
item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Lions blasted the Arizona Cardinals this past weekend, 45-21. Any time the opposition posts up close to 50 points on your club, it is a huge issue.

Except for the 26-14 victory over the hapless Los Angeles Chargers on opening weekend, the Cardinals’ defense has surrendered 31, 36, 36, and now 45 points.

RELATED:SHOULD THE CARDINALS TRADE JOSH SWEAT?

Maybe it’s just time to let DC Nick Rallis go.

The Cardinals have allowed a league-high 162 points in just five games. Every American Football team at every level wants to average scoring 32.4 points a game. That is a dream situation. For Arizona, that dream is currently a nightmare.

The Cardinals’ 1-4-0 record is indicative of their inability to keep opposing offenses out of the end zone.

Against the pass, Arizona’s defense has allowed the most passing touchdowns (14), tied for third with the fewest interceptions (3), ranked #32 in passing yards gained per attempt (9.1), second-worst defensive ranking (117.2), has allowed the third-greatest first-down conversion ratio (41.7%), given up the fourth most plays of 20+ yards (18), given up the fourth most plays of 40+ yards (3), and is ranked #14 in the most sacks (11).

Versus the run, the Cardinals are ranked #9 in total rushing yards (633), #9 in rushing attempts (144), tied for #4 in most rushing touchdowns allowed (6), tied for #10 in most yards per carry average (4.4), and allowed the tenth most first downs via the run (35).

According to FOX Sports, Arizona’s defense is ranked #26 overall. That is broken down into a #25 ranking for the passing defense and a #23 ranking for the run defense.   

What are the issues?

Against the Lions, the Cardinals’ defense forced three straight three-and-outs to begin the game. Then, it was a jailbreak, with Detroit scoring six touchdowns and a field goal. They scored 24 points in the second quarter and 14 in Quarter 3. Huge passing gains were rampant. And the pass rush? Should we say the lack of a pass rush? Only DT Roy Lopez was putting some pressure into Detroit’s backfield and had a good game against the run.

In the postgame press conference, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur didn’t act disappointed or sad; instead, he was pissed. Regarding the defensive effort, he stated:

“Obviously, not good enough. I know we’re better than that, but that doesn’t mean s*** right now.”

Before being hired as the head coach of the Cardinals, LaFleur and Rallis had no connection with past employment. While LaFleur has been situated along the West Coast, Rallis was mainly with the Philadelphia Eagles, coaching with former Arizona head coach Jonathan Gannon. LaFleur simply kept him as his DC.

But last year, the Cardinals defense wasn’t spectacular either. They finished the year ranked #26 overall, allowing an average of 363.4 yards a game. Both the run defense and pass coverage were in the bottom third in the league.

When Gannon hired Rallis, he was considered one of the brighter minds in the game with plenty of youth behind him. In 2025, The Athletic featured him in its “NFL 50 under 40” list of ascending coaches and front office personnel.

Right now, Arizona’s defense under Rallis is struggling to play at a level that gives the team a chance to win. What do four consecutive losses giving up 30+ points tell any Cardinals fan? No matter what this offense accomplishes, it is erased by the defense not being able to close out games late.

And this is not simply a one-off. Last year, the Cardinals had a late lead and lost in seven contests. Remember when the offense was down 14 points to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 4 only to come back and tie the game? Seattle got the ball back with just 28 ticks on the clock, then went bip-bip-bip before kicking the winning field goal. All the defense had to do was contain, then take the game into overtime.

Look at this year’s Seahawks game. Everyone in the league knows what to expect from Seattle WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba. He is a weapon, yet did Rallis give Smith-Njigba double coverage and force their offense to throw to other pass catchers? Hell no. What occurred instead was that the talented receiver had 155 yards and scored three touchdowns. He became the runner-up for “NFC Offensive Player of the Week.”

Against the Lions, where was the run defense? RB Jahmyr Gibbs ran willy-nilly on his way to 151 yards on just 25 carries with two touchdowns, then rarely got any coverage from a linebacker when he went out for a short pass. He had five receptions for 56 yards.

The Cardinals’ continued defensive struggles don’t seem to have an end game. Each week, it is going to be more of the same. Maybe a change at the top needs to be made and is in the franchise’s best interest to move on from Rallis.

Most NFL coaches and GMs will not reveal anything pertinent to almost every situation. In the presser, LaFleur was asked if any coaching changes are on the horizon after getting blasted for 45 points.

The question specifically was, “Do you need to make any changes to the defense coaching?”

LaFleur’s response:

“There’s a lot to fix right now, and I respect the question. I understand that, and I get it comes with the territory right now. My focus is on me fixing everything. None of it’s good enough. And again, anytime there’s a blowout like this, it starts with coaching. It’s not the players. It starts with us.”

Like always, just Hollywood talk without anything that has legs. And no head coach is going to come right out and say that one of his coaches is probably going to kick rocks. There is respect in this league, and it is a rarity to throw others under the bus. Plus, it is a decision that needs to be thought out first and discussed within the organization and not be decided on the spur of the moment at the podium after a bad loss.

And LaFleur is a guy who is going to point the finger at himself all day long.

During last week’s press conference, Rallis was asked about the weekly 30+ points per game. He said:

“Yeah, that sucks. Just focus on the process.”

Come again? That’s it? No resolutions to the issue? Now, we get that the offense has its own set of problems and such; the defense is on the field more than ideal. Players get winded, especially in the final quarter. But Rallis didn’t offer any solutions whatsoever.

And it isn’t going to get any easier. A glance at the schedule reveals upcoming games against the Los Angeles Rams, Denver Broncos, Dallas Cowboys, Seahawks, Rams, and then the Kansas City Chiefs. Raise your hand if you believe things will be different against these offenses.

In LaFleur’s first stint as an NFL head coach, he surrounded himself with veteran coaches on both sides of the ball. Rallis was already in Arizona, and it was an easy fix. But there is very little pass rush; the defensive backfield suffers from having to cover guys for way too long, minimal coverage from the linebackers on tight ends and running backs flaring out of the backfield, and the run defense is allowing 126.6 yards per game. Last season, they gave up 28.7 points on average per game, which ranked #29 in the league. 

DT Walter Nolen was brought in to solve the run defense and has been hurt repeatedly. Even though he is healthy this year, he has been a non-factor. DE Josh Sweat was the big splash signing and netted 12.0 sacks last year, yet is the invisible man with the pass rush this season. DE Darius Robinson is taking up space and getting a paycheck, and LB Zaven Collins is getting some pressure, but he isn’t an every-down pass rusher.

Defensive rankings under Rallis:

2023

Overall: #25

Passing: #13

Rushing: #32

2024

Overall: #21

Passing: #14

Rushing: #20

2025

Overall: #19

Passing: #7

Rushing: #31

2026

Overall: #26

Passing: #25

Rushing: #23

We get it that the Cardinals’ best pass defender, CB Will Johnson, is on IR and gone for the year. That is a huge loss. But life goes on. Games come up on the schedule and have to be played. Adjustments must be made, or free agent signings can happen.  

And what is the biggest head-scratcher is how GM Monti Ossenfort made minimal changes to the defensive roster in the offseason.

He should have re-signed DT Calais Campbell and his 6.5 sacks plus S Jalen Thompson, who was highly productive. Then, he should have taken one of the elite pass rushers with the third overall pick, and in Round 2 nabbed one of college football’s best tacklers, LB Jacob Rodriguez out of Texas Tech, who currently leads the league in total tackles. Why was LB Akeem Davis-Gaither let go? He is seventh in the NFL in tackles so far with the Indianapolis Colts.

Arizona has senior defensive coach Teryl Austin waiting in the wings, who offers years of experience coordinating a defense and has been successful as a DC on many clubs.

For each loss that places the Cardinals further down the division, it will only put more pressure on LaFleur to make a change.

Is it time for a bigger picture conversation?

item.title: Cowboys news: Dallas could be squandering the best years of Dak Prescott

item.content:encoded:
The Dallas Cowboys have had some good fortune with Dak Prescott as their quarterback, but it hasn’t been nearly enough during the best seasons of his career. Joey Porter Jr. dove into why he didn’t play against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and how much he could play versus the Green Bay Packers.

Team owner Jerry Jones and head coach Brian Schottenheimer seem to have different ideas about where Christian Parker will call plays from now on, and the Cowboys also released some midweek injury updates.

Are the Cowboys wasting prime years of Dak Prescott’s career? – Jon Machota, The Athletic

The Cowboys have made five playoff appearances with Dak Prescott as their quarterback. Their lack of building consistently good rosters have resulted in a lack of postseason success.

During Prescott’s first nine NFL seasons, the Cowboys were 76-46 when he started. Average that out over a 17-game season and that’s between 10 and 11 wins every year. It’s a record that basically means a playoff berth any time the franchise quarterback plays a full season.

Under head coach Brian Schottenheimer since the start of last season, the Cowboys have had the 33-year-old Prescott for every start. They are 9-12-1. Certainly not good enough to even make the playoffs.

Joey Porter Jr. explains sudden illness, hints at plan for him vs. Packers – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com

Joey Porter Jr. was abruptly sent home before th Cowboys played the Buccaneers last week. He speaks on what happened and what the outlook is for him in regards to playing time against the Packers.

“I really just couldn’t hold anything down,” he told DallasCowboys.com on Wednesday, after returning to practice. “You know, I just kept throwing up. I try to fight through. I tried to take a nap before the game, just to shake it off, but I just couldn’t hold in deep down.

“So that’s when they made the call to send me home.”

It certainly wasn’t for lack of effort that Porter missed the game. He took a nap to try and feel better after reporting to the team earlier in the day that he felt a little off, apparently then missing the team bus to the stadium and catching a rideshare to try and suit up.

Cowboys haven’t used their best weapons consistently in 2026. That needs to change soon – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News

Dallas averages a lot of points per possession on offense. However, their struggles on defense have limited their ability to score even more.

“You never want the defense on the field a lot,” Cowboys defensive tackle Kenny Clark said. “Our job is to get off the field.”

Therein lies the root of the Cowboys’ lack of offensive possessions. The Cowboys have been victimized often by long drives. The New York Giants set the tone for the season — and that game, notably — when they allowed a 10-play touchdown drive on their opening possession. That tone was echoed even louder when the Buccaneers, with an undrafted rookie quarterback, went on a 15-play scoring drive in last Thursday’s win over the Cowboys. item.title: Which injury return for the Lions will have the biggest impact?

Throughout the offseason, SB Nation will host NFL fan surveys, sponsored by FanDuel Sportsbook. For Pride of Detroit, we are tasked with fielding questions from Detroit Lions fans, and since the Lions are on a bye in Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season, we are shifting from our regular opponent-based question to a roster-focused one.

Here are our two questions for Lions fans this week:

  • Which Lions player returning from injury will have the biggest immediate impact? (weekly question)
  • Are you confident the Lions are headed in the right direction? (recurring poll)

Our recurring “confidence the Lions are headed in the right direction” survey results hit an all-time low in the Dan Campbell era last week, plummeting to a meager 12%. However, after hanging 45 points on the Cardinals in Week 5 and the defense showing signs of improvement, it’ll be interesting to see if this survey rebounds this week.

As for our new survey this week, the Lions are on the cusp of returning two key starters from injury in the next two weeks, as safety Brian Branch and center Cade Mays have opened their 21-day evaluation windows and could return as soon as Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers, as Campbell noted last week:

“They won’t have other teammates around, running plays and all that stuff, but they’re going to be here continuing to condition, get ready (during the bye week),” Campbell said on Friday. “As (much) football stuff as they can do without it being that with the training staff. Then let’s get them going Green Bay week. Let’s get them going, and then we’ll assess. Hopefully by midweek, we’ll have a pretty good idea (if they can return to play).”

Note: Since we’re looking a bit ahead this week, the Lions Week 7 opening betting line against the Packers, set by the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook, is already at Lions -3.5 points and could shift if the Lions can return Branch and Mays.

While each player’s return is still to be determined, our question this week hopes to uncover which Lions player returning from injury do fans think will have the most immediate impact?

When Branch returns, he should jump directly into a starting role, creating a rippling effect on the Lions secondary. However, Achilles’ injuries are notoriously difficult to return to form from, and it could be a while before we see the Pro Bowl version of Branch that Lions fans have become accustomed to.

Mays is also expected to step back into a starting role once he returns, but with Juice Scruggs playing well, might the Lions consider taking their time returning their prized free agent to play?

We have also added an “other” option for fans this week, in case anyone believes another player expected to return from an injury list this year might be more impactful. item.title: Mike Macdonald and Sean Payton beef, explained: Revisiting 2024 cheating dispute
item.description: Mike Macdonald and Sean Payton have a history. Here's a look back at Macdonald's viral comments about a cheating dispute in 2024.
item.content:encoded:
The Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks are guaranteed to play each other only once every four years.

It's the reality of a rotation-based schedule for two teams in different conferences. However, there is a lot of history between these two clubs – especially recently.

The Seahawks demolished the Broncos in Super Bowl 48. For an encore in 2022, Seattle fleeced Denver in the infamous Russell Wilson trade that helped rebuild the Seahawks into a Super Bowl contender again. There had been a lack of drama between the teams in the years since, who haven't played since Sept. 8, 2024 – another Seahawks' victory.

At least that was until Sept. 22, when a viral moment from an interview with Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald reignited that flame – if it was ever put out in the first place.

As both sides get set to meet on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 6, it's a reminder of the interesting history between these teams.

Here's a look at the beef between Macdonald and Broncos coach Sean Payton.

Mike Macdonald and Sean Payton beef, explained

The beef with Macdonald and Payton extends back to the last time the Seahawks and Broncos met. The 2024 matchup saw the Seahawks win, 26-20, but it was the way that Seattle won that sparked the controversy.

Macdonald spoke about what happened during an interview with Graham Bensinger that went viral. The coach told a story about how the Seahawks scouted the Broncos through training camp videos posted by fans in 2024.

"We play them our first game," Macdonald said. "Fans will post plays from training camp on Twitter, so it's like public knowledge.

"We took like 100 plays from their training camp."

Macdonald noted that the team used those plays they found on social media to scout the Broncos ahead of their Week 1 matchup in 2024.

Broncos coach Sean Payton caught wind of the situation during the season and, as Macdonald said, threatened to go public with his findings.

"[Payton] called [Seahawks general manager John Schneider] and basically threatened to come out publicly and do a whole Patriots Spygate type of thing. And I'm sitting there like, 'Oh my god, I'm like we didn't cheat.'

"He thought it was a Michigan thing and we had a plant. So we had to counter with him to say, 'Hey look, if you come out with this then we're gonna sue you because it's not true.'"

Macdonald said Payton backed down after that, comparing the situation to the Cold War, with both teams threatening to "push the button."

The coaches have seemed to be on good terms since, but it was unclear what would happen in the aftermath of the story going public.

Mike Macdonald apologizes to Sean Payton

Macdonald reached out to Payton and apologized for his viral comments, noting his comments weren't designed for public consumption.

"It's something that I didn't intend for public use," Macdonald told reporters on Sept. 23. "But I felt ​like it was the most appropriate thing to reach out to Sean and ​really just apologize to him."

Payton confirmed the conversation and indicated there ⁠was no lingering issue between the coaches.

"We spoke. He and I are good. Lord ​knows I've been in his position," Payton said on Sept. 23. "It allowed us to figure out ​how to handle our training camp relative to just videos. I don't think anything was intentional by fans, but at first, you're kind of thinking, ‘How could...' Then we did some research online of ​what was available, and that's kind of how we changed our policy."

The Broncos have since instituted a strict no-phone policy in the seating area during training camp.

Both coaches seem to have developed an appreciation for each other in the time that has passed, seemingly burying the hatchet on something that will just have to live in the past.

One way or another, this will be the first time that both teams have met since that game. It will be the latest chapter in one of the weirder rivalries of the modern era.

item.title: Fantasy football Start ‘Em, Sit ‘Em: 30 players to start or sit in Week 6

Week 6 of the fantasy football season is here, and fantasy managers everywhere are entering do-or-die mode.

Those who have dealt with injuries or underperformance through the first five weeks now face a challenging task: getting every start-sit decision right from here on out. That will be the only way for many to rekindle their hopes of competing for fantasy football championships.

Week 6 will present a tough task for fantasy managers, as it will mark the first, four-team bye of the 2026 NFL season. The Cincinnati Bengals and Detroit Lions, two of the league's most fantasy-friendly teams, will be out of action, increasing the need for streamers across leagues of any size.

So, who are the best players to start and sit in Week 6? Here's a position-by-position breakdown of players to trust and those to fade as the NFL season rolls on.

Fantasy football players to start in Week 6

Quarterbacks

  • Jordan Love, Green Bay Packers (vs. Dallas Cowboys)

Love has been remarkably consistent in 2026, throwing for exactly two touchdown passes in each of his five starts. That gives him a high, week-to-week floor while his three games with 300-plus passing yards show off his ceiling. Love faces a Cowboys defense that ranks dead last in defensive EPA per play this season, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats, so he should be poised for a potential boom week in a favorable matchup.

  • Jameis Winston, New York Giants (vs. New Orleans Saints)

Just like everyone expected, Winston hasn't yet lost across three starts with the Giants this year and has thrown three passing touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Saints are one of two NFL teams surrendering more than 30 points per game, along with the Cardinals, so Winston and the Giants could find themselves positioned for another strong offensive showing in Week 6.

  • Kirk Cousins, Las Vegas Raiders (vs. Buffalo Bills)

Cousins is another good streaming option. He threw only one touchdown pass against the Patriots last week, but he's already thrown for 12 across his first five games with the Raiders. The Bills have a leaky secondary that Cousins and Brock Bowers can exploit, so expect Cousins to post borderline QB1 numbers in what should be a high-scoring matchup.

Running backs

  • MarShawn Lloyd, Green Bay Packers (vs. Dallas Cowboys)

Lloyd emerged as Green Bay's preferred goal-line option in Week 5, powering in two rushing touchdowns in its 31-7 win over Chicago. The Cowboys have surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points per game (FPPG) to running backs this season, so don't be surprised if Lloyd works his way back into the end zone or surpasses his season-high 49 scrimmage yards.

  • Rhamondre Stevenson, New England Patriots (vs. New York Jets)

Stevenson is going to be thrust into the full-time, featured back role for the Patriots with TreVeyon Henderson set to miss time because of a high-ankle sprain. The Jets have allowed the fifth-most rushing yards to running backs this season (511), so Stevenson should have a quality outing and high volume in this matchup.

  • Rachaad White, Washington Commanders (at San Francisco 49ers)

While Jacory Croskey-Merritt led the Commanders in rushing yards against the Giants in Week 5, White actually out-snapped him, seeing action on 37 of the team's offensive snaps. Part of the reason for that? White is well-regarded as a pass-catcher, which should help him continue to earn that type of snap share and also position him to take advantage of a 49ers defense that has allowed a league-high 37 receptions to running backs this season.

  • Dameon Pierce, Philadelphia Eagles (vs. Carolina Panthers)

Pierce couldn't do much against the Jaguars' league-best run defense, but he gets a much easier matchup against the Panthers in Week 6. Carolina has surrendered the fourth-most FPPG to running backs this season and Pierce's bruising style will make him a threat to punch in a touchdown – provided Saquon Barkley (hamstring) remains sidelined.

Wide receivers

  • Carnell Tate, Tennessee Titans (at Indianapolis Colts)

Did Tate have just one catch last week after logging 145 yards the previous week? Yes. Is that type of inconsistency what we should expect from Tate? Maybe, but it's still hard to pick against him facing the Colts. Indianapolis just saw second-round rookie Germie Bernard post solid numbers against it and has allowed at least 33 points in three of its five games this season. Tate has boom potential and should be treated as a high-upside flex option.

  • Tre Tucker, Las Vegas Raiders (vs. Buffalo Bills)

Tucker could be a sneaky-good play this week. The Raiders wideout has averaged 5.6 targets per game this year and turned them into a respectable 54.8 receiving yards per game. Granted, some of that is skewed by his 119-yard outburst in Week 2, but his floor is higher than most other speculative flex plays. Tucker gets a favorable matchup against a Bills team that has struggled against receivers, so he could enjoy another breakout game.

  • Keon Coleman, Buffalo Bills (at Las Vegas Raiders)

Coleman was only officially targeted twice in the Bills' Week 5 overtime win over the Rams, but he saw more opportunities during the game that were wiped out by penalties. That was also a tough matchup for the third-year pro, and he will have an easier time against a Raiders secondary that allowed 13 catches for 229 yards and three touchdowns to Patriots wideouts in Week 5.

  • Kendrick Bourne, Arizona Cardinals (at Los Angeles Rams)

Bourne took over as the Cardinals' No. 2 receiver following the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade. The veteran led the Cardinals with 70 yards on five catches against the Lions and could deliver similarly solid production against the Rams in Week 6. Los Angeles has surrendered seven receiving touchdowns to wideouts this year, which is tied for the third-most league-wide.

MARVIN HARRISON JR. TRADE GRADES: Texans swing disaster deal with Cardinals

Tight end

  • Pat Freiermuth, Pittsburgh Steelers (at Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

The Buccaneers have allowed the ninth-most FPPG to tight ends this season and Freiermuth has logged four touchdowns in five games. As long as he remains a favorite target of Aaron Rodgers, Freiermuth should be a solid weekly tight end option.

  • Tyler Higbee, Los Angeles Rams (vs. Arizona Cardinals)

Higbee has re-emerged as the Rams' top receiving tight end with Terrence Ferguson sidelined. He has averaged 7.7 targets over his last three games and has recorded at least five catches and 62 yards in each outing. He should be able to feast against a Cardinals defense that has allowed the fourth-most FPPG to tight ends this season.

Defense/special teams

  • Denver Broncos (vs. Seattle Seahawks)

Denver's defense is dealing with injuries at cornerback, but it still has enough playmakers needed to generate sacks and create turnovers. Sam Darnold has logged seven turnover-worthy plays in 2026 thus far, per Pro Football Focus, so the Broncos should be able to rattle the veteran a bit on "Thursday Night Football."

  • Indianapolis Colts (vs. Tennessee Titans)

The Titans are averaging a league-low 11.6 points per game through five contests. Cam Ward has struggled throughout those and has thrown an interception in each of his last three games while having a season average of two sacks suffered per game. Ward's issues and Tennessee's offensive ineptitude will give the Colts a higher floor than usual, making them an ideal streaming target.

Fantasy football players to sit in Week 6

Quarterbacks

  • Aaron Rodgers, Pittsburgh Steelers (at Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

Some fantasy managers may be tempted to trust Rodgers as a streamer, given that he has thrown three touchdowns in three straight weeks. That said, the Steelers are facing a Buccaneers defense that blitzes 41.3% of the time, the third-highest mark in the league, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. Rodgers has a passer rating of just 78 against the blitz, per Pro Football Focus, so his ceiling in this matchup is lower than usual.

  • Jalen Hurts, Philadelphia Eagles (vs. Carolina Panthers)

The Panthers have allowed only five passing touchdowns this season and limited Jared Goff and a high-flying Lions offense to one passing score. Hurts is already a low-ceiling passer, so that matchup won't aid him. Neither will his recent rushing production, as the veteran is averaging just over 15 rushing yards per game over his last four outings.

  • Dak Prescott, Dallas Cowboys (at Green Bay Packers)

The Packers have been good against the pass this year, with 181 passing yards allowed per game, the fifth-fewest in the league. Add in that Green Bay hasn't allowed multiple passing touchdowns against it since Week 1 and this looks like more of a boom-or-bust spot for Prescott than a safe start.

Running backs

  • Braelon Allen, New York Jets (at New England Patriots)

Allen enjoyed the best game of his career in Week 5 against the Browns, but he will face a tougher test against the Patriots in Week 6. New England isn't missing as much talent along the defensive front as New York and has allowed the sixth-fewest rushing yards per game this season (90.8). Allen will have a large workload, but that may not mean much if he isn't able to barrel his way into the end zone.

  • Woody Marks, Houston Texans (vs. Jacksonville Jaguars)

Marks will take on a bigger workload with David Montgomery dealing with a "week-to-week" groin injury, but he has a brutal matchup in Week 6. The Jaguars are allowing the fewest FPPG to running backs this season and seem likely to slow down Marks, who is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry this season, between the tackles.

  • RJ Harvey, Denver Broncos (vs. Seattle Seahawks)

Sean Payton took over Denver's play-calling in Week 5. During that contest, J.K. Dobbins handled 18 carries while Harvey got just three. More notably, Harvey's target share dropped from an average of seven per game over his first three outings to just one in Week 5. If he isn't catching passes, Harvey can't be trusted, especially not against a quality Seahawks defense.

  • Omarion Hampton, Los Angeles Chargers (at Kansas City Chiefs)

Mike McDaniel and the Chargers seem content to continue rotating Hampton, Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal at the running back position. The trio has all effectively logged equal snaps over the last two weeks, so it will be hard for any to be more than a boom-or-bust flex play. The Chargers also have a banged-up and bad offensive line, so it's getting increasingly difficult to view Hampton as anything more than bench fodder.

Wide receivers

  • DK Metcalf, Pittsburgh Steelers (at Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

Metcalf just isn't jelling with Rodgers so far in 2026, as the star receiver has generated more than 40 receiving yards in just one outing. As long as Rodgers continues to prefer the quick passing game and targeting his tight ends over the middle of the field, Metcalf will be hard-pressed to be a big-time fantasy asset.

  • Jaylen Waddle, Denver Broncos (vs. Seattle Seahawks)

Waddle is in a similar boat to Metcalf. Bo Nix has had a rough start to the season, which has limited Waddle's upside, as he has recorded more than 35 receiving yards only once in five games. The former Dolphin remains a big-play threat, but he seems unlikely to have a big game facing a Seahawks defense that has allowed the third-fewest FPPG to receivers this season.

  • Rome Odunze, Chicago Bears (at Atlanta Falcons)

Odunze has a solid matchup against the Falcons in Week 6, but he's been too inconsistent to trust this season. Perhaps the return of Caleb Williams will spark him, but Odunze averaged just 2.5 catches for 47.5 yards across Williams' two starts thus far in 2026.

  • Jakobi Meyers, Jacksonville Jaguars (vs. Houston Texans)

The Texans have struggled to defend receivers this season, but they just put the clamps on the Titans in Week 5. That alone makes Meyers hard to trust. Add in that he has only eclipsed four targets in one game this season and it's hard to recommend firing him up, even in what looks like a favorable matchup on paper.

Tight end

  • Mark Andrews, Baltimore Ravens (at Cleveland Browns)

Andrews had a shot at a touchdown against the Falcons last week, but he dropped it. He then fumbled on his first catch of the game and eventually had a two-point conversion punched out of his hands. Andrews may still post modest production, but his recent track record doesn't inspire confidence. Neither does a matchup with a Browns team that has been middle-of-the-pack against tight ends this season.

  • Jake Ferguson, Dallas Cowboys (at Green Bay Packers)

Ferguson is averaging just 4.2 targets and 20.4 receiving yards through five games this season. He still has touchdown upside, but unless he finds the end zone, he won't be a viable fantasy option. That makes him too risky to trust, especially against a Packers team that has allowed the fourth-fewest receiving yards to tight ends this season.

Defense/special teams

  • New Orleans Saints (at New York Giants)

It's a tough week for defensive streamers, but it's hard to recommend backing the Saints, even against Winston. While the veteran quarterback is prone to turnovers, New Orleans has forced just five through five games to date. The Saints also rank bottom-10 in yards allowed and second-worst in points allowed, so the floor is too low to recommend trusting them here.

  • Chicago Bears (at Atlanta Falcons)

There could be some temptation to start the Bears defense, especially if Tua Tagovailoa suits up instead of Michael Penix Jr., who is dealing with a rib injury. But remember, we just saw Green Bay dismantle Chicago with its deep passing game. The Falcons have quality downfield threats like Drake London and Kyle Pitts who can test the Bears, so their floor is lower than most would hope for in a streamer.

item.title: Duke Football: Tar Heels On Deck
item.description: Who will get the Victory Bell this time?
item.content:encoded:
Rivalry Week has arrived. Duke (4-1, 1-1) versus North Carolina (3-2, 1-1) in the Battle for the Victory Bell on Saturday afternoon at 3:30 p.m. EDT at Wallace Wade Stadium. Television coverage will be provided by ESPN2. Duke opened as a 4.5-point favorite.

Duke is coming off a 28-25 loss to Georgia Tech in Atlanta while North Carolina beat Pitt 21-17 on the road in Pittsburgh.

During Monday’s press conference, Head Coach Manny Diaz was asked how the team is responding: “It doesn’t take much to refocus when it is this game…I thought the leadership was great last night, the energy was great last night. But you would expect it to be.”

Duke sophomore running back Nate Sheppard continues to have a great season. He currently leads the nation in rushing yards per game (148.6) and all-purpose yards per game (180.8). Sheppard is tied for fourth in total touchdowns with 11. Expect the Duke offense to run through Sheppard again Saturday afternoon. Can Duke successfully execute downfield pass plays to complement Sheppard? A few explosive pass plays would go a long way toward retaining the Victory Bell.

Injury Report: Duke lost kicker Cosme Salas and linebacker Elliott Schaper for the season this past week. Both injuries occurred in practice. Three significant names appear on the Blue Devils initial report as Questionable: Sheppard, Matt Craycraft, Evan Smith.

For North Carolina, defensive back Greg Smith is listed as Questionable as are defensive linemen Isaiah Johnson and Donovan Hoilette, Jr. Defensive back Tre Miller is Out.

Offense: The Tar Heels offense has benefited immensely in 2026 with the addition of Bobby Petrino as offensive coordinator and play caller. Petrino is an experienced offensive mind and a schematically solid coach who knows how to utilize playmakers. North Carolina has no shortage of playmakers, starting with wide receiver Jordan Shipp. Shipp, at 6’2” 200, is a big wide receiver who leads the Tar Heels with 26 receptions for 366 yards. C.J. Sadler is the second wide receiver. He has seven receptions for 107 yards.

North Carolina’s most talented position might be its tight ends. Six of eight passing touchdowns have been caught by the tight ends. Jelani Thurman has 22 receptions for 262 yards and four touchdowns, while Shamar Easter has six receptions for 122 yards and two touchdowns. Thurman is 6’6” 245 and can run. Easter is 6’5” 230.

At running back, Benjamin Hall leads the way with 55 carries for 276 yards, while Demon June has 37 carries for 143 yards and five touchdowns. Hall also has five receptions for 58 yards and two touchdowns so he is dangerous as a receiver out of the backfield.

That brings us to the quarterback. Billy Edwards, Jr. has completed 79 of 132 pass attempts for 1,069 yards and eight touchdowns against five interceptions. Edwards isn’t a star, but he is a solid quarterback who can deliver the ball to the North Carolina playmakers if given time. Duke must pressure Edwards to move him out of his comfort zone, making him hurry throws.

Duke Defensive Coordinator Jonathan Patke described the Carolina offense: “Their tailback is a really talented, big strong guy who can run through contact. He has been impressive all year. They have a tight end that can really go, he can block, he can run routes, he is one of their leading targets. Their (wide) receiver is one of the best in the ACC. They do a nice job featuring him in the offense.”

Defending the Carolina passing attack will be a tough assignment for the Duke secondary.

Players to Watch: Jordan Shipp, Jelani Thurman, Benjamin Hall

Defense: Head Coach Bill Belichick is a defense-first coach and North Carolina’s defense has improved steadily since his arrival in Chapel Hill. Manny Diaz commented, “Since sometime last October, they (North Carolina) have been playing really, really good defense. If you play good defense you have a chance to win week in, week out.”

Defensive lineman Xavier Lewis is a dominant pass rusher who leads North Carolina with 6.5 sacks for 42 yards. Linebacker Derek McDonald leads the team in tackles with 49, while defensive back Greg Smith III leads the team with three interceptions and a forced fumble.

Duke Offensive Coordinator Jonathan Brewer described the Carolina defense this way: “Their defensive line is very impressive. They were very impressive last year in person. They create a lot of havoc in the backfield. They don’t have to pressure a lot because their d-line is really good.”

Statistically, North Carolina is 11th in the ACC in rushing defense yielding 152 yards per game and 7th in the ACC in passing defense yielding 204.2 yards per game. The Duke offense will be able to move the ball against the Carolina defense so the key will be finishing drives.

The Blue Devils must finish drives in the red zone with touchdowns. It will take TDs to beat Carolina and retain the Victory Bell. Field goals are not going to cut it.

Players to Watch: Xavier Lewis, Derek McDonald, Greg Smith III

Prediction: In a close, hard fought game, the Blue Devils prevail with strong fourth-quarter play. Duke 25, North Carolina 19.

item.title: Boye Mafe has been a fantastic NFL free agency signing for the Bengals
item.description: Boye Mafe has been everything the Bengals hoped he woud be.
item.content:encoded:
On the first day of free agency in March, the Bengals made two splashes with signing edge rusher Boye Mafe and safety Bryan Cook. Both won Super Bowls with their previous teams, and both players are entering the prime of their careers.

In particular, Mafe has given the Bengals exactly what they paid for… and more. 

“Right now, it’s a mindset to go out there and show who I can be as a player,” Mafe said after Sunday’s win over Miami. “With the coaches trusting me to be that player, it’s up to me to uphold that in my end of the bargain.”

Mafe signed a three-year, $60 million deal with the Bengals in free agency. Through five games, Mafe has three sacks, five tackles for loss, four quarterback hits, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, and one pass defensed. Sunday in Miami, Mafe had a sack, a tackle for loss, two quarterback hits, and a pass defensed. Mafe also pressured Malik Willis and forced a wobbly pass that Jordan Battle intercepted. 

“He has a lot of juice, man,” defensive tackle BJ Hill said. “He can get after the quarterback. He can do it all. He’s the guy you want on your team. I knew we had something special when he got here. He’s a different cat,” Hill said. “He’s just different. That’s all I can say. You’ll have to ask him. He’s different. You love to have that energy. You love having guys like that.”

It’s also the stats you don’t see on Mafe that stand out. Mafe’s PFF grade Sunday was 88.0, the highest of his career. His second-highest was in Week 1 this season at 86.5.

In addition, Mafe’s 77.1 pass-rushing grade is tied for 13th among 103 edge players who’ve played in at least 20% of their team’s defensive snaps. Among all NFL players, his 25 pressures rank sixth.

Mafe is 27 years old, which is the same age Trey Hendrickson was when the Bengals signed him in free agency in 2021. But Mafe brings far more versatility than Hendrickson. He can defend the run, pressure the quarterback, and cause turnovers. Look no further than his strip-sack of Baker Mayfield in the fourth quarter of Week 1.

“He’s willing to do anything,” Zac Taylor said about Mafe. “Stop the run. Drop. Rush. Rush inside … That didn’t surprise me. That’s what we were banking on, that he’d give you that type of effort. He’s completely bought in.”

Finishing has been an issue for the Bengals’ defense in recent seasons. Who’s their closer? It’s a question we asked a lot in those recent seasons, but Mafe could be that for this team.

“He has come in and been extremely competitive from Day 1,” said left tackle Orlando Brown Jr., who faced Mafe in 2023 when Mafe was with the Seahawks and played against him throughout training camp this summer. “He’s just a really good and smart football player who knows when to show up. What’s most impressive is some of the clean wins that he has. He figures out a way to finish. That’s a sign of a great defensive end. It’s crazy. I feel like he has gotten better even since he got here.”

While Dexter Lawrence grabbed a lot of the headlines this offseason in the Bengals’ signings and trades, Mafe may turn out to be their most important signing. So far, the Bengals are getting a great return on investment with him.

item.title: The Bills won and still dropped a seed. Here’s who needs to lose in Week 6.
item.description: The Bills won but slipped to fourth in the AFC. Here's who we're rooting for in Week 6 to help Buffalo climb back up.
item.content:encoded:
That was a better outcome than the week before. It wasn’t easy getting there, but the Buffalo Bills outlasted the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night to keep their hold on the top spot in the AFC East — something they were in danger of losing after the New England Patriots took down the Las Vegas Raiders the day before. Now it’s the Bills’ turn to face the Raiders on Sunday afternoon in Las Vegas. 

Despite the win, the Bills slipped to the AFC’s fourth seed. The Kansas City Chiefs hold the top spot thanks to a bye week and no chance to lose. Baltimore, Jacksonville, and Buffalo all sit at 4-1, but only the Bills have a division loss, putting them on the bottom rung of that ladder. 

Here’s a look at how the conference stands right now: 

  1. Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) 
  1. Baltimore Ravens (4-1) 
  1. Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1) 
  1. Buffalo Bills (4-1) 
  1. New England Patriots (3-2) 
  1. Denver Broncos (3-2) 
  1. Las Vegas Raiders (3-2) 
  1. Cleveland Browns (3-2) 
  1. Pittsburgh Steelers (3-2) 
  1. Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) 
  1. New York Jets (2-3) 
  1. Indianapolis Colts (2-3) 
  1. Houston Texans (1-4) 
  1. Miami Dolphins (0-5) 
  1. Los Angeles Chargers (0-5) 
  1. Tennessee Titans (0-5) 

So, we know we’re rooting for Buffalo, but there are plenty of other games around the league — most of them before the Bills kick off. Let’s take a look at this week’s rooting interests and see where we might be able to get a little help. 

_____________________________________________________________________________ 

AFC East 

Buffalo Bills at Las Vegas Raiders 

Root: Bills 

It’s not like you needed to be told to root for here. The Bills need to keep winning, especially with New England refusing to go away. A win in Las Vegas would move Buffalo to 5-1 and keep them in control of the AFC East. And after watching what the Patriots did to the Raiders last week, there’s no reason Buffalo shouldn’t be able to take care of business. Go Bills! 

New York Jets at New England Patriots 

Root for: Jets 

Yes, we’re rooting for the Jets. New England is sitting just behind Buffalo in the division, and the Patriots have already benefited from the Bills’ loss to Baltimore. A Jets victory would give Buffalo some breathing room in the AFC East. We don’t have to like these New York imposters. We just need them to win one football game. 

Miami Dolphins — Bye 

The Dolphins are still looking for their first win, and they won’t be getting it this week. At 0-5, Miami isn’t exactly threatening Buffalo’s division lead, so we can enjoy a week without having to think much about them. 

_____________________________________________________________________________ 

Rest of the AFC 

Seattle Seahawks at Denver Broncos 

Root for: Seahawks 

Denver is another AFC team we’d rather see collecting losses than wins. Seattle is an NFC opponent, making this a fairly easy choice. A Broncos loss helps keep another potential playoff contender from gaining ground. 

Houston Texans at Jacksonville Jaguars 

Root for: Texans 

Jacksonville is currently sitting above Buffalo in the conference standings, and that’s reason enough to want the Jaguars to lose. Houston is a division rival for the Jags, so a Texans victory would also tighten up the AFC South race. Plus, a second win for Houston will bolster the Bills strength of victory score. 

Baltimore Ravens at Cleveland Browns 

Root for: Browns 

Baltimore is currently sitting ahead of Buffalo in the AFC standings, so we need the Ravens to start collecting some extra losses. A Cleveland win would knock Baltimore down to 4-2 and give the Bills a chance to move ahead of them in the conference standings. And since it’s a division game, there’s always the possibility of an upset.  

Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts 

Root for: Titans 

Indianapolis is the bigger concern in the AFC playoff picture, so we’ll take a Tennessee victory here. The Titans haven’t given us much reason to expect one, but that doesn’t mean we can’t ask. Every loss for a potential AFC wild-card competitor is useful. And, don’t forget, it would be helpful if the bottom feeder AFC teams were slightly better than the bottom feeder NFC teams when draft time rolls around next Spring. 

Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers 

Root for: Buccaneers 

Another easy AFC-versus-NFC decision. Pittsburgh is coming off a win over Indianapolis, and we’d prefer the Steelers not start building momentum of their own. Tampa Bay can help by sending them home with another loss. 

Los Angeles Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs 

Root for: Chargers 

Kansas City got to sit at home last week and watch everyone else play football. Now it’s time for the Chiefs to put that undefeated record on the line. The Chargers are also an AFC playoff contender, but Kansas City currently holds the conference’s top seed. We’re going to need someone to knock the Chiefs off that perch, and a division rival seems like a good place to start. Plus, I’m done rooting for KC – I hope I don’t have to again this season. 

_____________________________________________________________________________ 

NFC 

Chicago Bears at Atlanta Falcons 

Root for: Bears 

Buffalo hosts Chicago in December, so we’d like the Bears to start putting some more wins on their record before they make that trip. Chicago winning helps the Bills’ strength of schedule, and if Buffalo beats the Bears later this season, those victories will count toward strength of victory, too. The Bears are coming off a rough loss to Green Bay, so let’s hope they can bounce back against Atlanta. 

Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams 

Root for: Rams 

Buffalo just picked up a win over the Rams on Monday night. Now we’d like Los Angeles to start winning again, because every Rams victory makes Buffalo’s win look a little better in the strength-of-victory calculation. We wanted the Rams to lose last week. This week, we’re happy to cheer them on. 

Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers 

Root for: Packers 

Green Bay is another team Buffalo has on the schedule, with the Bills headed to Lambeau Field in December. That means we’d like the Packers to keep winning between now and then. A Green Bay victory helps Buffalo’s strength of schedule, and if the Bills can beat the Packers later this season, all those wins become part of Buffalo’s strength-of-victory calculation. So, as much as it might pain some of us, we’re pulling for the Packers on Sunday night. 

Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers  

Root for: Commanders 

San Francisco is still undefeated, so we’re going to pull for Washington to change that. Neither team is on Buffalo’s schedule, so there isn’t much at stake for the Bills in this one. But there’s no reason to help another conference’s top team stay perfect. 

Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles 

Root for: Panthers 

Philadelphia has already lost to Jacksonville, and we’d be perfectly happy to see the Eagles take another loss. Carolina winning also keeps an NFC contender from getting too comfortable. But, there’s really no reason to get too worked up over this game.  

New Orleans Saints at New York Giants 

Root for: Saints 

This one isn’t going to move the AFC standings, and there’s no major reason for Buffalo fans to get worked up about the outcome. We’ll take New Orleans simply because we are tired of the Giants trying to claim they are New Yorkers. Plus, you know, history. But, in all honesty, this is one of those games where we can live with either result. 

_____________________________________________________________________________ 

Teams on Bye: 

Cincinnati Bengals, Detroit Lions, Miami Dolphins, Minnesota Vikings 

_____________________________________________________________________________ 

The Bills took care of their business Monday night, but the win didn’t move them up the AFC standings. In fact, they dropped a spot. That’s what happens when the teams around you keep winning, too. 

This week gives Buffalo a few opportunities to get some help. Baltimore and Jacksonville both have division games, Kansas City has to face the Chargers, and New England gets another chance to put pressure on the AFC East race. There are plenty of results worth watching before the Bills even take the field Sunday afternoon. 

Of course, none of that help means much if Buffalo doesn’t beat Las Vegas. So, we’ll spend the early part of Sunday rooting for a few teams we don’t particularly like, before checking in for the only game that really matters.  

Go Bills!
